recipes.title: Generate or review a Paper event listener
when: the request asks for listener code
the request describes behavior that should happen on a Bukkit or Paper event
the request asks which event class to use

steps.action: Resolve target version, Paper support, API reference, guardrails, claim policies, and output requirements.
evidence: Paper support metadata for the target version
Paper API reference and Javadocs URL for supported versions
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not emit Paper dependency coordinates for an unsupported target version.

steps.action: Use event search for candidates, then verify event type names against the Paper API surface.
evidence: Event search result for the described behavior
Paper Javadocs type match for the selected event class
steps.stopIfMissing: Treat search results as candidates only; do not generate listener code for an event class not verified by the API surface.

steps.action: Search every referenced event, player, entity, server, scheduler, or component type/member name.
evidence: Paper Javadocs type search result for each referenced type
Paper Javadocs member search result for each referenced member label
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not invent API names; name presence does not prove behavior, nullability, or thread safety.

steps.action: Inspect official target-version documentation for the selected event and define each handler's mutation role, EventPriority, cancellation policy, and execution context. Priorities run LOWEST, LOW, NORMAL, HIGH, HIGHEST, then MONITOR; do not depend on an undocumented order between handlers at the same priority. Cancellation does not stop dispatch, so use ignoreCancelled = true only when the handler must not run for an already-cancelled event; otherwise inspect the event's current cancellation and mutable state. MONITOR handlers are observation-only and must not cancel or mutate the event.
evidence: Official target-version Paper event-listener documentation and Javadocs for EventHandler, EventPriority, and the selected event
A per-handler contract naming mutation or observation role, exact priority, prior-cancellation behavior, and execution context
Tests with an earlier listener that mutates or cancels the event before the handler under review
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not approve a listener whose priority, cancelled-event behavior, MONITOR role, or event-specific execution context is implicit.

steps.action: Give every listener registration a plugin and feature owner. Register stable listeners once during enable. For a dynamically enabled, replaced, partially initialized, or independently stopped feature, retain the exact listener instance and remove that instance from all handler lists; use plugin-scoped removal only for that plugin and never global listener removal. Inspect Event.isAsynchronous and event-specific documentation before touching Bukkit or Paper state: asynchronous dispatch may overlap and arrive in any order, and registration changes after dispatch starts do not affect that in-flight handler snapshot. Therefore unregistration is not proof that an already-running handler stopped; gate its side effects against current owner state and review any spawned task or player-session work under its own lifecycle concern.
evidence: Target-version member evidence for PluginManager.registerEvents, Event.isAsynchronous, and the selected HandlerList unregistration overload
An ownership table distinguishing plugin-wide, feature-scoped, and player-session-scoped listeners
Loaded-plugin tests for one-time enable registration, feature replacement or rollback, disable, and no invocation from subsequent dispatch after owned teardown
A controlled in-flight asynchronous callback test proving owner-state checks reject side effects after teardown
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not treat listener unregistration as cancellation of an in-flight callback or leave dynamic listener instances without an idempotent owner and teardown path.

recipes.failureMode: Generated listener code can target unsupported APIs, run at the wrong dispatch phase, mishandle prior cancellation, mutate at MONITOR, touch unsafe state from asynchronous dispatch, or remain active after its feature owner stops.

the request touches async work, scheduling, Folia, worlds, entities, or chunks

steps.action: Resolve the target version's Paper support, dependency coordinates, Javadocs URL, and scheduler/Folia documentation links.
evidence: Paper support entry for the target version
Paper API dependency and documentation links for supported versions
steps.stopIfMissing: State the Paper support gap instead of generating coordinates for unsupported latest Java versions.

steps.action: Search types and members in the target Paper API surface and fetch the surface if it is downloadable but missing locally.
evidence: Paper Javadocs type search result for each referenced type
Paper Javadocs member search result for each referenced member label
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not emit unverified type or member names.

steps.action: Use claim policies and Paper reference links to keep behavior, scheduler, and Folia claims bounded.
evidence: Paper type/member claim policy
Folia or thread-safety claim policy when scheduling, worlds, entities, chunks, or async work are involved
Paper scheduler and Folia documentation links when relevant

recipes.title: Own and stop Paper scheduled work safely
when: the request creates delayed, repeating, self-cancelling, or plugin-wide scheduled work
asynchronous I/O, futures, callbacks, or executors must publish a result through Bukkit or Paper APIs
reload, reconfiguration, feature shutdown, or plugin disable can replace or stop scheduled work
the request chooses between the Bukkit scheduler and Folia global, region, entity, or async schedulers
the request investigates duplicate loops, orphaned tasks, late callbacks, unsafe async API access, or work that survives teardown

steps.action: Resolve the target Paper version, inspect its official scheduler and lifecycle documentation, and search every scheduler, task-handle, cancellation, plugin-state, and lifecycle type or member used by the implementation. Verify BukkitScheduler, BukkitTask, Plugin lifecycle, and main-thread behavior for standard Paper. Inspect Folia scheduler documentation and target-version global, region, entity, async, ScheduledTask, cancellation, and retired-callback surfaces only when Folia support is in scope.
evidence: Target-version type and member matches for every scheduler, task handle, cancellation call, plugin-state check, and lifecycle method named in generated code
Official Paper scheduler documentation for synchronous main-thread execution, asynchronous execution, tick timing, and async Bukkit-access limits
Target-version Javadocs for plugin ownership, returned task handles, cancellation semantics, and any main-thread executor or Future behavior used

When Folia is explicitly supported, official Paper Folia documentation and target-version Javadocs for the selected global, location-region, entity, or async scheduler plus ScheduledTask cancellation and entity retirement behavior
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not invent a scheduler member, claim a cancellation or thread guarantee from a member label, or mark a plugin Folia-supported without target-version behavior evidence.

steps.action: Give every scheduled unit one plugin owner and one feature or component owner. Retain the returned task handle, or register it in an owned task group, whenever delayed or repeating work must stop before plugin-wide teardown. Give replaceable loops and async publication a lifecycle generation so reload or reconfiguration can invalidate earlier work. Treat custom executors, timers, futures, subscriptions, and child operations as separately owned resources because they are outside scheduler task ownership.
evidence: An ownership table mapping each one-shot, delayed, repeating, and child operation to a plugin, feature owner, task handle or task group, and lifecycle generation
An explicit early-stop path for feature disable, replacement, reload, reconfiguration, and terminal task conditions
A separate ownership and close or cancellation path for custom executors, futures, timers, subscriptions, and resources not created by the Paper scheduler
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not create untracked repeating work, replace a loop without invalidating its predecessor, or assume scheduler ownership also shuts down custom executors and child operations.

steps.action: Classify every task phase by execution context. Keep blocking I/O and expensive thread-safe computation out of the standard main thread or a Folia tick region. Treat Bukkit or Paper API access from asynchronous work as unsafe unless target-version behavior documentation explicitly permits it. Publish immutable results by re-entering the correct standard main-thread, Folia location-region, entity, or global context, then immediately revalidate the lifecycle generation, plugin admission state, and live target before side effects. Never wait on a scheduler Future from the main thread when the target Javadocs prohibit it.
evidence: An execution-context table for input capture, background work, result publication, and cleanup
A target-compatible scheduler choice tied to the state being accessed rather than a blanket global scheduler
A publication fence that checks lifecycle generation, plugin admission state, and target validity after returning to the required API context
No blocking wait, file or network I/O, or expensive computation on the main thread or a Folia tick region
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not move an entire workflow async, call world or entity state from an unverified thread, block a tick context waiting for completion, or publish after checking lifecycle state only when background work started.

steps.action: Make teardown idempotent and order it explicitly: close admission, advance or invalidate the lifecycle generation, cancel owned scheduled handles or task groups, cancel and close separately owned resources, and clear references. Treat cancellation as an attempt to prevent pending or future execution, not as proof that an already-running callback or child operation has stopped. Running work must observe the closed generation before its next side effect, and late background completion must be discarded instead of scheduling new publication after reload, replacement, or disable.
evidence: One idempotent teardown sequence shared by feature stop, replacement, reload or reconfiguration, partial startup failure, and plugin disable where applicable
Target-version cancellation evidence that distinguishes queued or future executions from a callback already running
A closed-generation or admission check immediately before every late publication or durable side effect
Bounded shutdown and reference cleanup for custom executors, futures, timers, subscriptions, and child resources
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not claim teardown is complete merely because cancel was called, and do not let already-running or externally owned work publish into a disabled or replacement generation.

steps.action: Use a controlled scheduler or clock for unit-level ordering and cancellation tests, then add the smallest target-version loaded-plugin evidence required for lifecycle or scheduler behavior claims. Test cancellation before first execution, self-cancellation of repeating work, replacement-generation invalidation, repeated teardown, disable with queued work, an async callback that finishes after cancellation, rejected late publication, and cleanup of separately owned executors or resources. When Folia support is claimed, test the selected ownership scheduler and relevant entity-retirement outcome instead of treating standard Paper tests as Folia evidence. Route per-player connection generations and durable player flush semantics to the dedicated player-session lifecycle guidance.
evidence: Deterministic tests for pending cancellation, repeating self-cancellation, generation replacement, double teardown, queued work at disable, and running async completion after cancellation
Assertions that late work performs no Bukkit, Paper, durable, messaging, or state side effect after its generation closes
Cleanup assertions for task handles, task groups, executors, child resources, and retained references
When claimed, target-version loaded-server or Folia evidence for lifecycle ordering, scheduler ownership, and entity retirement behavior
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not claim scheduler lifecycle safety from compilation, sleeps, or a normal repeating-task happy path; narrow the claim and list the missing runtime evidence.

recipes.failureMode: Scheduled work can duplicate after reload, access Bukkit state from the wrong thread, outlive its feature or plugin generation, leak custom executors, or publish after cancellation because ownership and teardown were implicit.

recipes.title: Generate or review loss-safe Paper item delivery
when: the request grants, rewards, restores, refunds, or otherwise delivers items to a player inventory
the implementation calls Inventory.addItem or another API that can leave items uninserted
the request asks what should happen when an inventory is full or only part of a stack fits
the implementation drops, persists, retries, or reports overflow items

steps.action: Resolve target Paper support, then verify every inventory insertion, fallback, ownership, and convenience member used by the delivery path.
evidence: Paper support metadata and API reference for the target version
target-version type/member matches for the selected insertion and fallback APIs
behavior documentation for partial insertion and the chosen overflow fallback
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not invent an insertion or fallback member, and do not assume Player.give exists or handles overflow the same way on every Paper version.

steps.action: Choose explicit complete, partial-with-recovered-fallback, deferred or rejected without mutation, and failed-with-undelivered-stacks outcomes before mutating the inventory.
evidence: one documented overflow policy for every uninserted stack
an explicit result contract that preserves uninserted stacks until one delivery outcome is complete
a pickup or ownership policy when overflow is dropped into the world
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not start a partial inventory mutation until every possible uninserted stack has one loss-safe outcome.

steps.action: Trace each requested stack into exactly one outcome, route only returned uninserted stacks to the fallback, and test capacity and retry boundaries.
evidence: complete-insertion, partial-insertion, and full-inventory tests
retry tests and selected fallback-failure tests that prove the original input is not processed twice
requested, inserted, deferred, and dropped or otherwise recovered item counts
steps.stopIfMissing: Treat the delivery path as unsafe until full-inventory and retry tests account for every requested item without loss or duplication.

recipes.failureMode: A delivery can report success while silently losing overflow items, or duplicate already inserted items when fallback and retry logic reuse the original input.

recipes.title: Generate or review safe Paper custom inventory GUI interactions
when: the request creates or reviews a custom Paper or Bukkit inventory GUI, menu, or chest interface
the request handles InventoryClickEvent, InventoryDragEvent, shift-click, number-key, hotbar, offhand, or double-click input
the request asks how to prevent protected GUI items from being moved, collected, swapped, or dragged

steps.action: Identify the owned custom view from its top-inventory holder or another stable identity, then cancel every InventoryClickEvent and InventoryDragEvent for that view before branching into allowed behavior.
evidence: Target-version API matches for InventoryClickEvent, InventoryDragEvent, InventoryView, and the chosen holder identity
A listener branch that scopes the entire open view and applies cancellation before any top, bottom, outside, slot, or click-type return
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not protect a GUI by title text or by top-inventory clicks alone; first define a stable owned-view identity and a default-deny policy for both events.

steps.action: Distinguish top, bottom, and outside clicks with the view, clicked inventory, and raw slot; keep GUI controls cancelled and allow only an explicit slot-and-action matrix. Deny cross-view or global mechanics by default, including shift transfer, number-key or hotbar swap, offhand swap, and double-click collect-to-cursor. Reject deprecated InventoryClickEvent.setCursor and verify any supported manual cursor mutation against target-version behavior documentation.
evidence: Target-version matches for clickedInventory, rawSlot, hotbarButton, ClickType, InventoryAction, and every supported cursor member used by the policy

An explicit decision for MOVE_TO_OTHER_INVENTORY, NUMBER_KEY, HOTBAR_SWAP, SWAP_OFFHAND, DOUBLE_CLICK, COLLECT_TO_CURSOR, outside clicks, every intentionally editable slot, and deprecated InventoryClickEvent.setCursor
steps.stopIfMissing: If any click source, click type, action, slot, or cursor mutation is not classified, leave it cancelled; never treat a bottom-inventory click as harmless merely because the clicked slot is outside the top inventory, and never use deprecated InventoryClickEvent.setCursor.

steps.action: Keep InventoryDragEvent cancelled unless every raw slot in the drag footprint is explicitly allowed; reject the entire drag when any raw slot is protected, outside policy, or spans a disallowed top/bottom boundary.
evidence: Target-version matches for InventoryDragEvent raw-slot and cancellation members
A subset check that requires all affected raw slots to be allowed rather than accepting a drag when only one slot matches
steps.stopIfMissing: If the complete raw-slot set cannot be proven safe, cancel the whole drag; do not partially accept a multi-slot drag.

steps.action: Before allowing editable top slots, choose per-session or deliberately shared ownership and define one atomic terminal transition for commit, close, replacement view, disconnect, death, or plugin shutdown. Capture and clear or persist each owned stack once, then return, commit, defer, or reject it with an explicit overflow outcome; repeated events and queued tasks must observe the settled state and do nothing.
evidence: A per-session or shared ownership model and an open-to-settling-to-settled transition that can succeed only once
Target-version matches and behavior documentation for InventoryCloseEvent, close reason, inventory reads and clears, player insertion, and every selected overflow fallback
Tests proving commit, close, replacement view, disconnect, death, shutdown, and repeated callbacks neither lose nor settle the same owned stack twice
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not allow player-owned items into an editable top slot until the session has one owner, one terminal settlement transition, and an overflow-aware outcome for every captured stack.

steps.action: Cancel before manually changing slots that the event would modify, and defer close, open, or reopen transitions from InventoryClickEvent, InventoryDragEvent, and InventoryCloseEvent handlers until the next supported scheduler turn. Revalidate the player, owned view, GUI session, and terminal settlement state before a deferred transition so stale tasks cannot reopen, mutate, or settle a replaced view.
evidence: Paper event behavior documentation for in-handler inventory mutations and view transitions from InventoryClickEvent, InventoryDragEvent, and InventoryCloseEvent
A target-compatible next-turn scheduler choice and stale-view, session, and terminal-state guards before deferred close, open, or reopen work
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not call closeInventory, openInventory, inventory close, or view close directly inside click, drag, or InventoryCloseEvent handling, and do not queue a reopen that can race with settlement, disconnect, plugin shutdown, or another view.

recipes.failureMode: A custom inventory GUI can leak, duplicate, steal, or move protected items when alternate click paths, multi-slot drags, deprecated cursor mutation, repeated settlement, shared ownership, or stale close/reopen tasks bypass a top-slot-only handler.

recipes.title: Generate or review an operable Paper administrative command
when: the request adds or reviews an administrator, moderator, operator, configuration, or maintenance command
the feature needs state mutation plus list, show, status, reload, retry, repair, reset, grant, revoke, or remove operations
sender context, explicit targets, offline handling, permissions, failure feedback, or bulk scope are unclear

steps.action: Write an operation matrix before choosing syntax. Classify required create or change, remove, list, show, status, reload, retry, repair, reset, unlock, and recovery actions, and record the intentional alternative for any required action that is not a command. Keep secrets in a dedicated secret, environment, or protected configuration path rather than command input.
evidence: An operation matrix with syntax, mutating or read-only classification, sender contexts, target kind, permission, outcome categories, and verification path
An explicit decision for configuration reload, effective-state inspection, failure recovery, and safe retry
For each non-command alternative, its safety reason, authorization, validation, verification, and recovery procedure
A secret-input decision that keeps raw secret values out of command arguments, suggestions, histories, logs, results, status output, and audit records
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not leave a required action dependent on an undocumented out-of-band procedure. A deliberate file, secret-management, startup-only, or restart procedure must explain why a command or hot reload is unsafe and document authorization, validation, verification, and recovery.

steps.action: Choose sender support from actual input and trust needs. Permit console when no player-local input is required; enumerate the target-version dispatchable CommandSender subtypes, including player, local console, remote console, command block, command minecart, proxied, and custom senders, explicitly allow or reject each with feedback, and reject unknown or future subtype fallthrough by default. Require an explicit target for privileged subject operations, distinguish online-only live-state targets from offline-capable persistent targets, resolve names to stable known identities without treating an OfflinePlayer value as proof of prior registration, and make bulk scope deliberate.
evidence: Target-version matches for every CommandSender subtype, Player, OfflinePlayer, selector, identity, and lookup API used

A sender and target matrix covering local console, remote console, player, command block, command minecart, proxied and custom senders, unknown-subtype fallback, explicit rejection feedback, self, other subject, online, supported offline, missing, and bulk targets
A stable-identity policy that distinguishes a known offline subject from unknown or never-registered input
A preview or confirmation policy for destructive or all-target mutations
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not make an operation player-only without player-local input, silently accept or reject non-player sender kinds, let an unknown sender subtype fall through a generic executor, use the invoker as an implicit administrative target, or require an online Player for a persistence-only change.

steps.action: Assign and enforce an explicit least-privilege permission policy for every privileged branch. Parse targets, identifiers, counts, amounts, ranges, modes, and optional values with typed bounded arguments; treat suggestions and command visibility as usability only. Route secret-bearing values through a protected non-command mechanism and never echo raw secrets into feedback or diagnostics.
evidence: A permission node or equivalent policy, documented default, and denial test for every privileged branch
Typed argument bounds, optional defaults, target suggestions, explicit bulk scope, and proof that secret values do not enter the command surface
Execution-time authorization independent of suggestion filtering or command discovery
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not rely on operator status, hidden syntax, tab-completion filtering, or an unchecked parent command as the only protection for a privileged branch, and do not accept raw secrets as command arguments.

steps.action: Represent expected outcomes explicitly. For reload, parse and validate a complete candidate before one atomic publication, preserve the last valid state on failure, and serialize or version concurrent reload and mutation work. Keep file, database, and network I/O off the main server thread, publish Bukkit-facing state in a target-compatible execution context, and make retry idempotent or expose duplicate and partial results.
evidence: A typed result model for success, missing target, invalid input or state, denial, partial completion, conflict, and I/O failure
A last-known-good reload test that proves invalid input cannot replace effective state
A concurrency and scheduler decision for I/O, Bukkit state changes, reload publication, and retry
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not clear or partially replace effective state before full validation, and do not report a partial mutation as unconditional success.

steps.action: Return a bounded result to the invoker for every path, independently decide whether to notify the affected target, and provide list, show, or status output for the effective state. Record security-sensitive changes without secret inputs or values and test every supported and rejected sender, target, denial, failure, retry, and bulk boundary.
evidence: Success and failure messages addressed to the actual invoker, including console and administrators acting on another subject
A separate target-notification policy and a bounded non-secret audit record for sensitive mutation
List, show, or status output proving the effective post-change state

Tests for local and remote console, player, command block, command minecart, proxied and custom senders, unknown-subtype fallback, explicit sender rejection, self, other target, online, offline, missing, denied, invalid, I/O failure, rollback, retry, partial completion, confirmation, and secret redaction
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not leave the invoker to infer completion from target notification, logs, or a later restart, and do not expose secret input or values in arguments, suggestions, histories, results, status output, logs, or audit context.

recipes.failureMode: Administrative code can compile while remaining unusable or unsafe in production because its command surface omits sender, target, permission, inspection, atomic reload, recovery, or observable-result contracts.

recipes.title: Model stable player identity and intentional display names in Paper
when: the request stores, resolves, searches, or displays a Minecraft player
Paper code uses UUID, Player, OfflinePlayer, PlayerProfile, account names, nicknames, or displayName components
a player rename, disconnect, cache miss, or cross-server update could make identity or presentation stale
a player-facing message, inventory, dialog, tab list, scoreboard, title, or notification may expose an internal identifier or unintended name source

steps.action: Inventory every player-related value and surface before choosing APIs. Separate stable identity used for ownership and persistence, mutable operator input used for lookup, current account name, optional plugin-defined display label, and the final Component or text shown on each human-facing surface.
evidence: A value-flow table from command or event input through lookup, storage, cache, and output
A presentation matrix for chat, inventory, dialog, tab, scoreboard, title, logs, audit, and external transports that are in scope
An explicit label for each value as stable identity, lookup input, account name, display label, or rendered output
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not use a generic name or displayName field when its identity and presentation semantics are not defined.

steps.action: Choose a stable player identifier from the authenticated identity boundary for keys, ownership, references, and joins. Treat account names and display labels as mutable attributes. An authenticated online-mode profile or correctly configured trusted proxy may provide rename-continuous identity; a direct offline-mode server does not authenticate an account boundary, so require an independently authenticated account link or state that rename continuity cannot be guaranteed and never auto-remap ownership from a name alone. Resolve human input to a known identity through an explicit exact-match policy, distinguish online, known offline, unknown, invalid, and lookup-unavailable outcomes, and do not treat an OfflinePlayer object alone as proof that a player is known.
evidence: Target-version matches for Player, OfflinePlayer, PlayerProfile, and the member signatures that carry UUID, profile, and lookup values
A storage schema whose primary player relationships survive account-name changes

An authentication and proxy-forwarding decision that identifies which UUID source is authoritative, whether rename continuity is actually guaranteed, and how offline-mode or identity-mode changes are migrated
For direct offline mode, an independently authenticated account-link design or an explicit no-rename-continuity limitation that forbids automatic ownership remapping
A typed resolution result covering online, known offline, unknown, invalid, ambiguous when applicable, and unavailable
A decision for exact matching, normalization, name history, and stale aliases
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not persist a mutable account or display name as the only player key, and do not silently create state for unresolved input.

steps.action: Choose the intended label independently for every human-facing surface: current account name, plugin-defined display label, a disambiguated combination, or name-free wording. Keep rich Component values distinct from plain lookup strings and treat untrusted names and labels as text instead of markup. For each transport, define encoding, escaping, mention behavior, newline and control-character handling, plain-text serialization, and which Component click or hover events may survive. Define null and unavailable fallbacks, and expose raw UUIDs only where an explicit machine-integration, diagnostic, audit, or operator contract needs them.
evidence: A documented source and fallback for every displayed player label

Tests proving that Component styling is preserved on rich-text transports, untrusted labels are not parsed as markup, external mentions or Markdown or HTML are escaped by policy, unsafe control characters and Component events are handled, and presentation is not reused as a lookup or persistence key
A deliberate decision for duplicate or visually identical labels and whether a secondary account name is shown
An audience and privacy decision for UUIDs, historical names, machine integrations, and operator-only diagnostics
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not pass Player.name, OfflinePlayer.name, displayName, UUID, or a fallback chain into user-facing output without an explicit presentation contract.

steps.action: Define the authoritative source for each stable-identity mapping, account-name attribute, and optional display label. Perform external profile, database, or network lookup off the main server thread with timeouts and bounded caches, publish results in a target-compatible context, and define refresh or invalidation on join, rename discovery, profile change, reconnect, and cross-server update.
evidence: A source-of-truth and revision or invalidation policy for multi-server or cached identity data
Timeout, negative-cache, retry, and stale-data behavior for external or remote lookup
A scheduler decision separating blocking lookup from Bukkit-facing publication
A convergence test for reconnect or updates observed on another server
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not block the main thread on profile lookup or allow independent caches to overwrite newer identity or display data without an ordering rule.

steps.action: Test identity and display behavior as state transitions rather than a single online happy path. Cover account rename, direct offline-mode limitations, known offline player, never-seen input, null or unavailable name, duplicate, markup-like, mention-like, newline, control-character, and event-bearing display labels, stale cache, cross-server update, reconnect, lookup timeout, and every output transport in scope.
evidence: Tests proving that a rename retains ownership and references where authenticated identity or an independent account link supports continuity, or proving the declared direct-offline limitation otherwise
Tests proving unknown input cannot masquerade as a known offline player
Snapshot or structural assertions for each user-facing transport and its fallback
Tests proving stale or failed lookup has a bounded, observable result
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not approve a player identity or display change using only a currently-online, unchanged-name example.

recipes.failureMode: Player data can attach to the wrong subject, disappear after a rename, leak raw identifiers, or show inconsistent labels when stable identity, lookup input, and presentation are treated as one interchangeable name.

recipes.title: Design or review a safe Paper plugin message, custom payload, or RPC protocol
when: the request sends or receives a Paper plugin message or custom payload
the request designs an RPC, binary protocol, message codec, request correlation, or response envelope
the request implements chunked upload, retries, timeouts, or connection-scoped protocol state

steps.action: Resolve Paper support for the target version, inspect the official Paper plugin-messaging documentation, and verify every transport type, registration call, listener signature, send call, and size constant used against the target Paper API surface.
evidence: target-version Paper support and Javadocs URL
target-version type/member matches for the transport APIs actually used

target-version member matches for Messenger.MAX_CHANNEL_SIZE and Messenger.MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE when they are used as transport ceilings, plus any StandardMessenger validation member referenced by the implementation
official plugin-messaging documentation for incoming/outgoing registration, byte-array transport through a connection or player, and lifecycle behavior
verified listener connection-state handling because a callback can represent a configuration-stage connection rather than a joined player
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not invent transport members or copy a documentation example or StandardMessenger transport validation as proof of a safe application codec. Do not hardcode protocol limits from memory; use verified target-version API constants or explicit lower project policy backed by evidence.

steps.action: Use namespaced registered channels with explicit enable/disable lifecycle, and define one versioned envelope with explicit request, response, error, cancellation, chunk, and control message kinds.
evidence: documented channel namespace and registration ownership
an envelope table covering version, message kind, request identifier, operation, payload, and terminal outcome
explicit compatibility behavior for unknown versions and message kinds
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not overload one implicit payload shape or accept unregistered, non-namespaced, unknown-version, or unknown-kind traffic.

steps.action: Decode with exact input consumption and reject malformed, truncated, trailing, unknown, or non-canonical data; validate byte, string, list, map, nesting, declared decompressed, and allocation sizes before allocating, and enforce an actual-output cap throughout decompression.
evidence: codec contract with exact-consumption and unknown-field behavior
limits for every attacker-controlled length, nesting depth, decoded collection, declared and actual decompressed body, and allocation
boundary and hostile decoder tests for empty, truncated, trailing, oversized, deeply nested, compressed, and unknown data
steps.stopIfMissing: Reject before allocation when a declared or derived size exceeds its bound, and never start decompression unless actual output is capped and aborted at the configured limit.

steps.action: Bind authorization and the acting player to the authenticated connection or explicitly trusted proxy boundary, scope request IDs to that connection/session, and define duplicate handling with at most one terminal response.
evidence: authorization matrix derived from trusted connection identity rather than a claimed payload player or UUID
connection/session-scoped request correlation and duplicate/idempotency state
separate transport error and business outcome envelopes with one terminal response per accepted request
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not assume every callback has a joined player, authorize from payload identity, reuse request IDs across sessions, retry undeclared non-idempotent operations, or emit both success and failure terminals for one request.

steps.action: Bound concurrent requests, chunks, uploads, queued bytes, and work; verify chunk ordering, checksum, declared total size, completion, expiry, and backpressure; clean state on timeout, cancellation, reconnect, connection close, and plugin disable.
evidence: per-connection and global concurrency, byte, chunk, upload, queue, timeout, and expiry budgets
an explicit unavailable-transport outcome because plugin messaging requires an eligible live connection or player carrier rather than a durable standalone server transport
cleanup tests for cancellation, timeout, reconnect, close, and disable
execution plan that keeps blocking I/O and heavy decoding off the server thread and publishes Bukkit state only in an API-safe context
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not retain orphaned request or upload state, accept unbounded work, block the server thread, or publish Bukkit state from an unsafe execution context.

recipes.failureMode: An underspecified plugin-message protocol can trust spoofed identities, allocate or decompress attacker-controlled sizes, duplicate side effects, leak connection state, or stall the server thread.

recipes.title: Own and tear down Paper player-session state safely
when: the request creates per-connection Paper player state, tasks, subscriptions, listeners, pollers, UI viewers, cooldowns, or caches
Paper code reacts to join, quit, kick, connection close, transfer, reconnect, plugin reload, or disable
an asynchronous callback or persistence write can complete after a player reconnects or a plugin stops
the request investigates leaked player sessions, stale Player references, duplicate cleanup, or lost durable state

steps.action: Resolve the target Paper version, then search its Paper type and member surfaces before naming lifecycle events or scheduler APIs. Treat event search as candidate discovery only. Verify any PlayerQuitEvent, PlayerKickEvent, PlayerConnectionCloseEvent, AsyncPlayerPreLoginEvent, transfer, or scheduler surface actually used, and inspect target-version documentation for ordering, cancellation, and phases. Do not assume every signal fires: define a fallback reconciliation sweep over the plugin's authoritative session registry and current connection state.
evidence: Target-version Paper type and member matches for every lifecycle event and API named in generated code
Target-version documentation evidence for event phase and ordering claims

For Paper 1.21.11 only after that verification: PlayerQuitEvent represents departure for a player who joined, PlayerKickEvent carries cause information, and PlayerConnectionCloseEvent follows PlayerQuitEvent for logged-in players and a successful AsyncPlayerPreLoginEvent but is not emitted for cancelled pre-login
A coverage table mapping quit, kick, transfer when relevant, connection close, failed or cancelled login, plugin disable or reload, and missing or late signals to cleanup triggers and reconciliation
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not invent a transfer event, scheduler call, lifecycle member, or guarantee that a candidate event fires in every connection phase.

steps.action: Separate durable player data from per-connection transient state. Give each accepted connection a new opaque session instance or monotonic generation in addition to stable player identity and plugin lifecycle epoch. Own tasks, subscriptions, listeners, pollers, UI viewers, transient cooldowns, caches, callbacks, and reverse indexes through that session object rather than a UUID-only map, and avoid retaining Player references outside the live session boundary.
evidence: A state model distinguishing durable player records, live session instances or generations, and the plugin lifecycle epoch
An ownership table for every task, subscription, listener, poller, UI viewer, cooldown, cache entry, callback, and reverse index
No long-lived Player reference in durable records, global callbacks, or completed-session state
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not approve session resources stored only by player UUID because a rapid reconnect can reuse the key while old work is still completing.

steps.action: Record each acquired session resource immediately. If initialization fails partway, dispose completed acquisitions in reverse order. Use one idempotent close path with an explicit state transition so quit, kick, transfer when relevant, connection close, plugin disable or reload, initialization failure, reconciliation, and repeated or late signals can all request cleanup safely. Cancel owned work, unregister or close owned resources, remove reverse indexes, and clear references even when an earlier cleanup action fails.
evidence: A session state machine whose close transition is safe to invoke more than once
An acquisition ledger and reverse-order partial-initialization rollback
Cleanup assertions for cancellation, unregistration, closed viewers, cleared reverse indexes, removed references, and independently reported cleanup failures
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not spread cleanup across event handlers without one idempotent owner and a partial-initialization rollback path.

steps.action: Every asynchronous callback must capture only stable input plus the originating session generation and plugin epoch. Before publishing a result, reacquire the current player or target through a target-version-supported API in the required execution context, verify that the plugin is still accepting publications and that the current session generation matches, then discard or redirect stale results. Cancellation is not sufficient because already-running work may still complete.
evidence: A publication guard comparing player identity, session generation, and plugin lifecycle epoch
A documented target-compatible execution context for Bukkit or Paper-facing publication
A test in which an old callback completes after reconnect and cannot mutate or message the new session
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not publish an async result from a captured Player reference, UUID-only lookup, or plugin state that was checked only when work started.

steps.action: Define ordered durable persistence separately from transient teardown. Use a monotonic revision or idempotency key so late writes cannot overwrite newer state, bound queueing, retries, and flush time, and specify transfer and reconnect semantics. During plugin stop, stop accepting new sessions and publications, close sessions, await already-owned writes behind an explicit shutdown barrier, perform bounded final flushes where the host contract permits them, and expose timeout or recovery state instead of starting fire-and-forget work after disable.
evidence: A per-player write-order contract using revisions or idempotency keys
A bounded shutdown sequence with admission closed before a barrier waits for in-flight persistence
Explicit semantics for same-server reconnect and proxy or server transfer, including whether durable state is handed off, reloaded, or revision-checked
An observable timeout, retry, journal, or recovery decision when persistence cannot finish within the shutdown budget
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not claim durable shutdown safety when writes are unordered, unbounded, or launched after plugin disable without a host-owned completion barrier.

steps.action: Run a bounded reconciliation sweep that finds sessions whose connection or plugin epoch is no longer current and closes them without relying on one perfect event sequence. Observe active sessions, resources acquired and disposed, close reasons, repeated cleanup, rejected late callbacks, persistence queue age, shutdown-barrier timeouts, and leaked sessions or reverse-index entries. Test lifecycle races and missing signals. Item or inventory contents, ownership settlement, and transactional delivery are outside this concern; route those to their dedicated inventory or delivery guidance.
evidence: Tests for rapid reconnect, an old callback after reconnect, double cleanup, partial initialization failure, transfer semantics, disable with in-flight persistence, and missing or late lifecycle events
A reconciliation test that removes an orphaned session and all reverse references
Metrics or structured logs that make nonzero leaked-session and stale-publication counts actionable
A scope statement excluding item or inventory contents and ownership settlement
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not approve lifecycle handling based only on a normal join followed by one quit event.

recipes.failureMode: A UUID-only session map or event-only cleanup path can leak resources, let old callbacks mutate a replacement connection, retain stale Player references, or lose and reorder durable state during reconnect, transfer, reload, and shutdown.

recipes.title: Own, arbitrate, and reconcile Paper BossBar audiences
when: the request creates or reviews a Paper BossBar whose viewers change over time
several feature-owned bars can compete for one intended UI slot
viewer eligibility depends on session, backend, permission, world, range, visibility, or owner state
scheduled or asynchronous work updates BossBar content or audiences
bars must close safely across replacement, reconnect, transfer, reload, or plugin disable

steps.action: Resolve the target Paper version, then verify the BossBar type, creation surface, addPlayer, removePlayer, getPlayers, removeAll, setVisible, every lifecycle event, and the scheduler context actually used. Read official behavior prose after checking the bundled type and member surface. Treat the API index as name evidence only, prefer non-deprecated target members, and do not infer ownership, arbitration, thread safety, event order, or cross-server cleanup from method presence.
evidence: Target-version type and member matches for every BossBar, lifecycle, and scheduler API named in generated code
Official Javadocs behavior evidence for adding, removing, listing, hiding, and detaching viewers
A statement that plugin-owned generation, stable arbitration, lifecycle coverage, and any distributed handoff are application policies rather than guarantees derived from the BossBar member list
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not invent a BossBar member, lifecycle event, execution-context guarantee, removal operation, or backend handoff behavior when target-version evidence does not establish it.

steps.action: Define a stable logical slot key and exactly one current owner generation for each bar. Keep the bar handle, candidate state, current winner, desired and applied viewer identity sets, writer, revision, plugin epoch, and terminal state under that owner. Before ranking or attaching a viewer, evaluate all declared gates from current state: owner active, plugin accepting work, current player session and backend, permission, world, range, visibility, and any other product rule. Store stable identities and immutable facts, not long-lived Player references.
evidence: A state diagram for active, replacing, closing, and closed owner generations
An ownership table for the bar handle, candidates, winner, viewer identities, reverse indexes, queued commands, and cleanup
An eligibility table naming every gate, its authoritative source, reevaluation trigger, and terminal behavior
No Player object in candidate, queued, cached, desired, applied, reverse-index, or durable state
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not create or publish a bar whose owner generation, complete eligibility predicate, or terminal owner is ambiguous.

steps.action: If product design allocates one logical slot to competing candidates, filter to currently eligible candidates, rank by declared priority and an immutable stable tie-break key, and retain the current eligible winner until an explicit switch rule is met. Define hysteresis with controlled monotonic time and bounded values, such as separate enter and exit thresholds, a minimum hold interval, or a priority switch margin. Specify immediate terminal exceptions and behavior when no candidate remains. If simultaneous bars are intended, model separate slots instead of imposing one winner globally.
evidence: A total ordering with explicit priority direction and a stable final tie break independent of map or callback order
A bounded hysteresis contract covering enter, remain, switch, leave, owner termination, and no-candidate outcomes
Controlled-time examples proving rapid enter and leave does not flicker while a materially better or sole eligible candidate can take over
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not let hash iteration, event arrival order, equal scores, wall-clock timing, or threshold noise choose or repeatedly switch the visible candidate.

steps.action: After owner and winner selection, compute one authoritative desired Set of stable viewer identities from current eligibility. In the target-version-verified Paper context, snapshot current attached players for that bar without retaining the list, derive current-minus-desired removals and desired-minus-current additions, remove first, then reacquire and revalidate each desired live player immediately before adding. Record the successfully applied identity set and independently report failures or drift; repeated reconciliation with unchanged inputs must be idempotent.
evidence: Set-diff tests for add, remove, unchanged, disconnected, newly eligible, newly ineligible, and actual-viewer drift cases
Removal-before-add ordering and a final eligibility check using the current session and backend generation
An assertion that repeated reconciliation performs no duplicate side effects and retains no Player references
Viewer add and remove counters whose imbalance or nonzero post-close viewer count is observable
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not append viewers opportunistically, rely on only enter or leave events, or treat a cached applied set as authoritative when the actual bar can drift.

steps.action: Route title, progress, style, winner, visibility, and viewer mutations through one writer for the logical slot in the verified Paper execution context. Every accepted immutable command carries the logical slot, owner generation, plugin epoch, and a strictly increasing slot revision. At application time reject a noncurrent generation or epoch, a revision at or below the applied revision, and every publication after closing begins. Bound pending count and memory per slot and across the manager, coalesce replaceable updates by slot and newest revision, and reserve admission and prompt execution for terminal cleanup.
evidence: A single-writer invariant and documented target-compatible publication context
Revision-order tests covering duplicate, out-of-order, old-generation, old-plugin-epoch, and post-terminal commands
Configured per-slot and aggregate command-count and memory bounds plus coalescing behavior for replaceable updates
An overload test proving terminal hide and detachment cannot be dropped or indefinitely delayed
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not mutate the same logical bar directly from listeners, tasks, and callbacks or use an unbounded queue whose pressure can starve cleanup.

steps.action: Use one idempotent terminal transition for owner or feature completion, encounter end, an owning player-session close, rapid reconnect or relevant backend transfer, replacement, partial initialization failure, reload or disable, repeated signals, and orphan-owner reconciliation. A non-owning viewer-session end only invalidates that viewer and runs audience reconciliation; it does not close a shared owner. For terminal cleanup, close update admission, mark the generation terminal, hide through a verified visibility member, detach every current viewer, clear desired and applied sets, candidate state and reverse indexes, and close the writer. Continue independent cleanup after one action fails, retain no Player objects for retry, and release the last bar handle only after detachment is confirmed or a bounded observable cleanup-failure outcome is recorded. Publish a replacement only after old-generation detachment is confirmed; otherwise reject or defer it with the cleanup failure visible. On transfer of a session-owned bar, start a fresh local generation and use an explicit plugin-owned fence or handoff policy; Paper BossBar methods do not establish distributed ownership.
evidence: A terminal-cause matrix covering owner or encounter end, owning-session close, reconnect or transfer, replacement, initialization failure, reload, disable, repeated signals, and missing signals, plus viewer-only reconciliation for a non-owning session end
Replacement ordering evidence showing the old generation hidden and detached before the new generation publishes
Idempotent cleanup assertions for zero attached viewers, empty desired and applied sets, no reverse indexes, a closed writer, and no retained bar or Player references after successful detachment
A bounded observable failure path that stays terminal, continues independent cleanup, retains no Player objects, and does not claim zero leaks when detachment cannot be confirmed
An explicit local-versus-distributed ownership and transfer policy without an automatic Paper handoff claim
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not consider a generation closed while it remains visible, has attached viewers or reverse references, accepts updates, or can be reached by an old callback.

steps.action: Test pure eligibility, ordering, hysteresis, set-diff, generation, and revision rules with controlled time and callback order. Add the minimum target-version loaded-server or client evidence needed for actual BossBar attachment and visibility claims. Cover rapid enter and leave, equal-priority ties, winner replacement, same-identity reconnect, backend transfer, repeated disable, stale generation and revision callbacks, queue overload, partial initialization, missing or late lifecycle signals, orphan reconciliation, and zero viewers or reverse indexes after every terminal path. Report which tests prove plugin policy and which prove Paper or client behavior. Keep boss AI, encounter mechanics, custom mobs, ModelEngine, scoreboard, action bar, and vanilla /bossbar authoring outside the result.
evidence: Deterministic unit tests for gates, total ordering, hysteresis, set differences, revisions, and idempotent terminal state
Lifecycle race tests for rapid threshold changes, replacement, same-identity reconnect, transfer, repeated disable, stale callbacks, overload, and missing signals
Leak assertions showing zero attached viewers, active generations, pending commands, reverse indexes, and retained Player references after closure
Exact target-version runtime commands and a limitations statement for visibility or lifecycle behavior not exercised on a loaded server or client
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not claim flicker-free, leak-free, transfer-safe, or client-visible behavior from only compilation, immediate-success unit tests, or mocked Paper internals.

recipes.failureMode: Unowned or independently updated BossBars can oscillate, accumulate viewers, publish stale state into a replacement, and survive reconnect, transfer, owner completion, or plugin shutdown.

recipes.title: Preserve semantic identity and unrelated state when updating Paper ItemStacks
when: the request recognizes, compares, refreshes, or migrates a plugin-defined ItemStack
custom items currently rely on material, custom name, lore, item model, custom model data, or rendered appearance for identity
display text or model data must change without erasing enchantments, attributes, damage, persistent data, data components, or another system's state
an item schema changes and older inventory, container, entity, or persisted stacks must be upgraded safely

steps.action: Define one stable plugin-owned namespaced or domain item identifier and a separate explicit schema or migration version. Store them in target-version-supported custom persistent data rather than deriving identity from Material, custom or display name, item name, lore, item model, custom model data, tooltip styling, or client rendering. Material may be an invariant checked after identity is known, but material alone is not a logical custom-item key. Treat a missing, malformed, foreign-namespace, or unknown identifier as an unknown item with an explicit unchanged outcome.
evidence: A stable logical item-ID registry with a plugin-owned namespace and no presentation-derived keys
A separate current schema version plus typed outcomes for known-current, known-old, unknown, malformed, unsupported-future, and failed migration
Target-version Paper or Bukkit type/member evidence for ItemStack, ItemMeta, NamespacedKey, PersistentDataHolder or PersistentDataContainer, and the exact accessors used
Official Paper documentation evidence that persistent custom data is namespaced and that lore or display-name storage is collision-prone
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not recognize or migrate a custom item until its stable logical ID, version key, unknown-item outcome, and target-version storage APIs are explicit.

steps.action: Define three independent questions: whether two stacks carry the same logical item ID, whether they are eligible for the application's stack, merge, grouping, or comparison operation, and whether a particular client/resource-pack context renders them alike. Current ItemStack.isSimilar documentation describes equals without amount, so use it only when that complete metadata comparison matches the required decision; never substitute it for logical identity or visual equality. Conversely, matching logical IDs do not prove similar gameplay state or identical presentation.
evidence: Separate predicates or typed decisions for logical identity, application stackability or similarity, and visual comparison
Target-version documentation for ItemStack.equals, ItemStack.isSimilar, amount handling, and every other comparison API used
Tests where equal logical IDs have different damage or presentation, different logical IDs render alike, and amount-only differences exercise the chosen similarity rule
A statement that server-side metadata cannot prove client-rendered visual equality
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not use ItemStack.isSimilar, Material equality, or apparent rendering as a universal custom-item identity predicate.

steps.action: Acquire ownership before mutation: clone the ItemStack or otherwise prove the caller owns the instance when another inventory, cache, template, event, or subsystem may share it. Mutate the owned copy in place through target-version-supported meta APIs instead of reconstructing it from Material. Replace only a documented presentation allowlist owned by this feature, such as the chosen custom or item name, lore, item model or custom model data, tooltip style, or render flags. For a list-valued field such as lore, declare whole-field ownership or a persisted structural composition contract that identifies an owned segment without rendered-text matching; if neither exists, leave that field unchanged. Preserve amount, enchantments, attribute modifiers, damage, unbreakable and other gameplay state, every unowned PDC key, identity and version keys, custom or unknown data components, subtype-specific metadata, and all unlisted state unless a named migration explicitly transforms it. When getItemMeta returns a copy, apply it back; when an API returns a component snapshot, set the changed component back; inside editMeta, interact only with the provided meta as its Javadocs require.
evidence: An ownership boundary showing when an ItemStack is cloned and when the updated copy replaces the original reference
A closed presentation-component allowlist, explicit whole-field or structural ownership for list-valued presentation, and a default-preserve rule for every field outside it

Target-version Javadocs evidence for ItemStack cloning or copying, getItemMeta or editMeta, setItemMeta, custom or item name, lore, item model or custom model data, and component snapshot behavior actually used
Before-and-after structural tests proving enchantments, attributes, damage, amount, unowned PDC keys, owned identity, unrelated data components, subtype metadata, and unknown state remain equal
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not refresh presentation by constructing a new stack or selectively copying remembered fields, mutate a possibly aliased ItemStack in place, or edit lore when line ownership would have to be inferred from rendered text.

steps.action: Dispatch migration by the stable logical ID and stored schema version. Run deterministic one-version steps on a private working copy, reject unsupported future or malformed versions, validate the result, and write each new version only after its transformation succeeds. Publish the migrated copy only after the full requested chain succeeds, leaving the original unchanged on failure. A current-version item must be a no-op, repeating migration must produce the same state, unknown items must be returned untouched, and presentation refresh must canonically replace owned lore or other fields instead of appending on every run or deleting lines by duplicate display text.
evidence: An ordered migration registry keyed by logical item ID and exact from-version
A private-copy commit boundary that leaves the source unchanged after exceptions, rejected validation, unknown ID, malformed version, or unsupported future version
Tests proving current-version and repeat migration are idempotent, every supported old version reaches the same canonical current state, and version markers never advance after a failed step

A duplicate-lore test set proving canonical whole-field-owned lore does not accumulate and, when structured sharing is supported, an identical unowned line outside the owned segment survives without text matching
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not mark an item current before its migration succeeds, mutate unknown items speculatively, or make display-text replacement the migration selector.

steps.action: Test the identity and update functions as value transformations with exact structural snapshots. Cover duplicate and visually identical lore, repeated presentation refresh, repeated migration, missing or malformed identity, unknown and unsupported-future items, failed intermediate migration, alias isolation, amount differences, same-ID but nonsimilar stacks, different-ID but visually identical stacks, and preservation of every unrelated state category. Add a target-version loaded-server test when correctness depends on Paper applying ItemMeta, PDC, subtype metadata, or data-component behavior rather than only plugin-owned pure logic.
evidence: Pure tests for ID and version dispatch, no-op current state, repeat migration, unknown untouched, failure rollback, duplicate lore, and comparison decisions

Structural preservation assertions for amount, enchantments, attributes, damage, unbreakable state, unowned PDC, custom data components, subtype metadata, and all out-of-scope state represented by fixtures
An aliasing test showing updating one clone or owned copy does not mutate a template, cache entry, or separate holder
Loaded target-version Paper evidence for API semantics not fully observable in pure code, with exact version and limitations
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not approve the updater from a single freshly-created item whose only metadata is the expected name and lore.

recipes.failureMode: A presentation refresh or migration can misrecognize an item, erase unrelated gameplay or third-party state, mutate aliased templates, duplicate lore, or advance a schema marker after partial failure when ItemStack identity and ownership are implicit.

recipes.title: Design a lifecycle-safe Paper plugin configuration
when: the request creates, loads, saves, migrates, reloads, or reviews Paper plugin configuration
a plugin exposes a configuration reload command or applies changed settings without a restart
configuration controls schedulers, listeners, caches, clients, repositories, files, credentials, or other runtime resources
startup, reload failure, concurrent reload, external file edits, or plugin disable could leave effective state unclear

steps.action: Inventory every default resource, operator-edited file, generated state file, secret source, schema version, migration, immutable effective snapshot, and runtime resource derived from configuration. Define the owner, source of truth, read and write path, mutability, startup behavior, hot-reload support, restart-only keys, redaction policy, and disable cleanup for each. Keep operator configuration separate from generated runtime state when they have different ownership or durability rules.
evidence: A configuration inventory covering defaults, operator input, generated state, secrets, schema and migration ownership, effective snapshots, and derived resources
The exact target Paper version plus official plugin-configuration, command, and JavaPlugin Javadocs used for lifecycle semantics
A key-level decision for startup-required, safely hot-reloadable, and restart-required settings
A source-of-truth and write-ownership decision that prevents operator edits and plugin writes from silently overwriting each other
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not add a reload path until file ownership, the effective-state boundary, and every derived runtime resource are known.

steps.action: Extract packaged defaults only with non-replacing semantics, then read the operator file through a bounded path and distinguish missing, unreadable, malformed, unsupported-schema, migration-failed, and semantically invalid outcomes. Parse into a typed immutable candidate, apply explicit versioned migrations, validate all fields and cross-field invariants, and only then make the plugin ready. Keep blocking file work away from the server thread using a target-compatible lifecycle and scheduling design; gate commands, listeners, tasks, and publications until initialization has either committed a valid snapshot or failed closed with an actionable non-secret error.
evidence: Target-version evidence for every JavaPlugin, configuration, lifecycle, and scheduler API named by the design
Typed startup outcomes that do not confuse an empty fallback configuration with a valid operator file
A readiness state machine that prevents partially initialized services from observing absent or mutable configuration
Tests for first run, an existing operator file, missing defaults, unreadable input, malformed syntax, semantic invalidity, unsupported schema, migration success, and migration failure
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not publish a default, empty, partially parsed, or partially migrated configuration merely because the configuration API returned an object.

steps.action: Provide an explicit plugin-owned reload operation instead of relying on the deprecated server-wide reload or Paper's own configuration reload. Serialize reload requests or assign monotonic revisions, read and fully validate a detached candidate off the server thread, then prepare replacement resources without exposing them. Recheck the source revision and plugin lifecycle epoch before one target-compatible commit swaps the immutable snapshot and prepared resource bundle. Retire old resources only after the commit; if preparation or commit fails, close the candidate resources, preserve the previous snapshot and resources, and report a typed failure. When side effects cannot be made atomic, define ordered compensation and a degraded-state outcome rather than claiming rollback that the implementation cannot perform.
evidence: A prepare, commit, retire, and compensation state machine with one visible configuration generation
A last-known-good test proving invalid input and candidate-resource failure cannot replace effective state
A concurrency test proving an older slow reload cannot publish after a newer accepted revision
A command contract distinguishing plugin configuration reload from the deprecated server-wide reload and Paper server-configuration reload
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not call a reload transactional when validation mutates live state, readers can observe a partial update, or failed candidate resources can displace the last known good state.

steps.action: Have consumers capture one immutable configuration generation per operation rather than sharing a mutable FileConfiguration. For schedulers, listeners, caches, clients, repositories, and long-running callbacks, define whether they retain their starting snapshot, are recreated during commit, or reject stale publication by comparing generation and plugin epoch. Reject hot changes to restart-only keys before commit. Reconcile additions, removals, and changed limits as one ordered resource plan, and make disable or a concurrent reload cancel candidate work and close both prepared and retired resources exactly once.
evidence: A consumer matrix for snapshot capture, recreation, stale-result rejection, and restart-only keys
An ownership ledger for tasks, listeners, caches, clients, repositories, files, and prepared or retired resources
Tests for disable during reload, late callback after reload, repeated close, partial preparation, retirement failure, and changed scheduler or cache settings
A bounded degraded-state and operator-recovery decision when retiring an old external resource fails after commit
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not mutate one shared configuration tree in place or assume every existing task, cache, connection, and callback automatically adopts the new values safely.

steps.action: Treat the on-disk operator file as desired input and the committed immutable snapshot as effective state. Do not save a stale cached configuration after an external edit. If the plugin must write operator configuration, require a known source revision or fingerprint, apply a typed change to that version, serialize without secrets or generated state leakage, write a temporary file in the same trusted directory, durably replace the destination where the platform supports it, and feed the resulting revision through the same validation and commit path. Otherwise keep runtime-generated state in a separately owned store and leave operator configuration read-only.
evidence: A desired-versus-effective state model and a policy for external edits during programmatic saves
A compare-before-write or single-writer contract that prevents stale in-memory state from clobbering a newer operator file
Crash and conflict tests around temporary-file write, replacement, reload of the written revision, and recovery
A separate protected source and redaction policy for credentials and secret material
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not use saveConfig as an unconditional persistence step when another actor can edit the file or the in-memory object may be stale.

steps.action: Expose a permission-protected status surface with readiness, effective schema and generation, non-secret source fingerprint, last attempt and successful commit times, restart-required differences, degraded resources, and a bounded redacted error summary. Return a typed reload result to the actual invoker. Test lifecycle and ordering with controlled I/O and task completion, then use a loaded target-version Paper server to verify bootstrap, command registration, scheduler integration, reload publication, and disable behavior that pure tests cannot prove.
evidence: Status and reload-result assertions for success, invalid input, conflict, restart required, I/O failure, preparation failure, commit failure, degraded retirement, and plugin stopping
Deterministic tests for concurrent reload, older completion, file change during read, disable during preparation, stale consumers, and idempotent cleanup
Loaded-server evidence for target-version enable, readiness, command registration, reload commit, and disable transitions
Exact commands, target versions, results, known baselines, skipped checks, and limitations without config values or secrets
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not report reload success from file parsing alone; prove which generation and derived resources became effective and disclose any degraded or restart-required state.

recipes.failureMode: Configuration can appear to reload while partially updated services, stale cached writes, racing generations, leaked resources, or unreported restart-only settings leave runtime behavior different from the file and status output.

recipes.title: Design and evolve Paper persistent data contracts
when: the request stores plugin data in PersistentDataContainer on an item, entity, block entity, chunk, world, structure, raid, player-related view, or another PersistentDataHolder
Paper code creates NamespacedKey values or custom PersistentDataType adapters
persistent data must be copied, moved, removed, replaced, serialized, or migrated between schema versions
a PDC read fails because a key is missing, uses a different primitive type, or contains malformed complex data
data appears to vanish after holder conversion, block-state mutation, unload, reload, restart, or plugin upgrade

steps.action: Resolve the target Paper version, inspect the target Paper type and member surfaces for every holder and PDC method actually used, and read the current official PDC guide and matching Javadocs for behavior. Record version gates instead of copying the latest ItemStack APIs into older targets: the current Paper guide documents a read-only ItemStack PDC view from 1.21.1 and editPersistentDataContainer from 1.21.4, while older targets use ItemMeta paths. Treat API indexes as name evidence only and make no thread-safety or save-timing claim that the holder documentation does not establish.
evidence: Target-version matches for NamespacedKey, PersistentDataHolder or PersistentDataViewHolder, PersistentDataContainer or its read-only view, PersistentDataType, and every holder-specific read or publication member used
The official Paper PDC guide for holder coverage, version-gated ItemStack access, read-only views, explicit cross-holder copying, and TileState update behavior: https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/pdc/
Matching target-version Javadocs for has, get, getOrDefault, set, remove, copyTo, and custom type behavior when those members are referenced
A statement of unverified holder lifetime, save, scheduler, or thread assumptions
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not invent a writable OfflinePlayer PDC, retain the temporary container supplied to an ItemStack edit consumer, assume a latest-version convenience exists on an older target, or infer thread safety and persistence timing from a method name.

steps.action: Define a closed data dictionary before writing: one reusable plugin-owned NamespacedKey per field or record, an explicit cross-plugin namespace contract only when another plugin intentionally owns or consumes the key, the exact PersistentDataType primitive and complex representations, nullable or default behavior, semantic validation, size and nesting bounds, and compatibility policy. The current Paper guide lists byte and byte array, double, float, integer and integer array, long and long array, short, string, Boolean convenience, nested tag-container, list, and custom-adapter forms; verify the target supports every selected form instead of assuming the latest set. Distinguish has(key), which checks only key existence, from has(key, type), which checks only the stored primitive type. A custom type backed by BYTE_ARRAY still matches any byte array at that key, so validate length and contents after decoding; get and getOrDefault do not turn a present wrong-type entry into absence.
evidence: A key registry naming namespace owner, key path, holder scope, primitive type, complex type, optionality, default, bounds, schema version, and readers or writers
Explicit outcomes for absent key, present expected primitive, present incompatible primitive, malformed custom payload, unknown enum or identifier, and unsupported schema version
Custom PersistentDataType round-trip and malformed-input tests that validate payload shape rather than relying on has(key, type)
Documented maximum bytes, elements, nesting, string length, and accepted numeric range before allocation or domain publication
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not use unnamespaced or foreign keys by accident, treat has(key) as type validation, treat primitive-type agreement as custom payload validity, or decode unbounded arrays, lists, strings, and nested containers.

steps.action: Map each record's required lifetime and ownership to a verified holder, then document how mutations become authoritative. Prefer read-only PDC views for inspection. Keep an ItemMeta or holder snapshot inside its valid scope and publish through the target-version-supported write-back path; keep the container passed to ItemStack.editPersistentDataContainer inside its consumer; call the required TileState update after changing its snapshot. Treat OfflinePlayer PDC as read-only unless a separate documented writable owner exists. Do not expect PDC to transfer automatically when an item becomes a placed block, an entity is replaced, or data moves to another holder; copy only the intended owned keys and define source deletion, destination conflict, and retry outcomes.
evidence: A holder-lifetime table covering creation, read, mutation publication, save or unload boundary, replacement, deletion, and reload or restart
Target-version loaded-server evidence that the selected ItemStack, ItemMeta, TileState, Entity, Chunk, World, Structure, Raid, or other holder path persists through its required boundary
A transfer contract with selected owned keys, destination collision policy, source-retention or source-removal rule, retry or idempotency behavior, and failure recovery
Tests proving no implicit PDC copy is expected between distinct holders
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not mutate a detached snapshot without publishing it, use a read-only view as a write path, hold an edit-consumer container after the callback, assume every block has a TileState, or delete source data before destination publication is verified.

steps.action: Store an explicit schema version with each independently evolved record. Parse and validate old data into an owned in-memory model, apply a bounded sequence of one-version migrations, validate the complete target state, then publish data and advance the version only after success. Preserve or reject unsupported-future data without speculative rewrites.
