Prefer one nested tag container for a record when replacement must avoid partially updated top-level fields; otherwise define a recovery marker or idempotent resume path because PDC is not a transaction. set overwrites the same key and rejects null, so remove with remove. copyTo copies custom keys and its replace flag controls destination collisions; use it only when whole-container copying is intentional, otherwise copy an explicit allowlist of owned keys and never clear or overwrite foreign namespaces.
evidence: A finite migration table from every supported old version to the current schema, plus explicit missing, malformed, and future-version outcomes
A staged publication design in which validation and all migration steps succeed before the current version marker becomes visible
An owned-key copy, replace, and removal matrix that distinguishes same-key overwrite, replace=false collision preservation, replace=true overwrite, source retention, and foreign-key preservation
Repeat-run, partial-failure, and recovery tests proving migrations and transfers are deterministic and idempotent
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not increment first and migrate later, coerce malformed data silently, downgrade an unsupported-future record, pass null to set as removal, or use whole-container copy or clearing when only the plugin's owned keys should change.

steps.action: Test the contract below Paper-facing code as pure codec and migration logic, then test the real target-version holder adapters. Cover every supported primitive and custom adapter used, wrong primitive under a known key, malformed and oversized payloads, absent optional and required fields, nested and list bounds, all supported old versions, unsupported future versions, repeated migration, failure before version publication, selective and whole-container copy collision policies, explicit removal, holder replacement, unload or save when relevant, reload or restart, and recovery after interrupted multi-key publication. Use a loaded target-version Paper server for holder snapshot, update, serialization, or lifecycle behavior that pure tests and API indexes cannot prove. ItemStack logical identity, comparison, and presentation refresh are outside this storage-contract concern.
evidence: Pure round-trip, compatibility, bound, migration, and copy-policy tests with exact structural assertions
Loaded target-version Paper tests for each holder-specific publication and persistence boundary actually claimed
Reload or restart fixtures containing current, supported-old, absent, wrong-type, malformed, oversized, and unsupported-future records
A recovery test that cannot expose a current schema marker with incomplete data and preserves unknown or foreign keys
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not approve a persistent format from a single successful set/get test in memory or claim restart, holder-transfer, snapshot, update, or thread behavior that the completed evidence cannot observe.

recipes.failureMode: An implicit PDC contract can misread a present value, erase another namespace, publish half a migration, lose data at a snapshot or holder boundary, or make malformed and future records unrecoverable.

recipes.title: Design or review a bounded server-backed paged Minecraft UI
when: a Paper inventory, menu, protocol-driven client screen, or other Minecraft UI displays a server-backed collection
the request mentions pagination, paging, infinite scroll, load more, next page, an opaque cursor, or a fixed result limit
a list silently truncates records, fetches all records before slicing, duplicates rows, skips tied rows, or appends a stale page
the UI must survive query changes, reopen, reconnect, insertion, deletion, or a shrinking final page

steps.action: Name the authoritative service or repository boundary, viewer and authorization scope, filter and sort inputs, stable record identity, and a total order with a unique tie-breaker. Choose either an opaque cursor or keyset contract whose exact position and query binding remain server-owned, or an explicit snapshot or revision contract for numbered pages. State whether results are a stable snapshot or a live feed and document the insertion and deletion behavior that choice can actually guarantee.
evidence: A page-contract table naming viewer scope, authorization, filter, sort, null and collation rules, stable record ID, unique tie-breaker, and snapshot or live-feed semantics
A cursor or revision design bound to the complete query and ordering rather than a client-editable row offset
Explicit guarantees and limitations for insertions and deletions before, inside, and after the current page
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not add page controls around an unstable or non-unique order, and do not call a cursor snapshot-consistent unless the server binds and verifies a snapshot or revision that provides that guarantee.

steps.action: Fetch at most one bounded page plus only the bounded lookahead or count evidence required by the chosen contract at the database, repository, or service boundary. Project the fields needed for that page in bounded batches. Do not fetch an unbounded collection into plugin memory, slice or take a fixed prefix afterward, or hide additional records without a continuation or terminal result.
evidence: A repository or service API that accepts the bounded page request instead of returning the complete collection
Query or adapter evidence that the requested page, lookahead, projection, and related-field work stay within explicit row, byte, and call bounds
A result path that distinguishes continuation, terminal exhaustion, empty data, and failure instead of silently truncating
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not describe a list as paged when the backend still loads every matching row or returns only a hard-coded prefix with no way to reach the remainder.

steps.action: Each request carries a current viewer or request generation plus the complete query identity and expected cursor or revision. Return bounded items, nextCursor or an equivalent opaque continuation when applicable, explicit exhausted state, and the accepted snapshot or revision when the consistency contract uses one. Represent initial loading, ready, loading more, empty, error, retrying, reset, and exhausted as distinct states so an empty first page, a failed next page, and a successful terminal page cannot collapse into one ambiguous boolean.
evidence: Request and response shapes containing generation or correlation, query identity, cursor or revision, items, nextCursor or equivalent continuation, and exhausted semantics
A UI state transition table for initial loading, ready, loading more, empty, error, retrying, reset, and exhausted
A documented page-size policy with an explicit bound and validation, without treating one fixed size as universally correct
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not infer end-of-list solely from a short or empty response unless that is an explicit server contract, and do not represent loading, empty, error, and terminal exhaustion with one nullable list or boolean.

steps.action: Accept a response only when its viewer generation, query identity, request correlation, direction, and predecessor cursor or revision match the currently expected transition. Make duplicate delivery idempotent, deduplicate retained rows by stable item ID, and define what happens when the same ID reappears with changed payload: reject the inconsistency under a snapshot contract, or apply an explicit monotonic version and replace rule under live-feed semantics. A live replacement must preserve ordering when sort fields are unchanged and intentionally reposition or reset when an ordering field changes. Reject reversed, skipped, out-of-order, and late pages, and stop with a typed error when a nonterminal response repeats or cycles a cursor instead of advancing it. Never append an old response to a replacement query or reopened viewer.
evidence: An acceptance predicate comparing current generation, query, correlation, expected predecessor, direction, and revision immediately before publication

Idempotent duplicate-page behavior and stable-ID deduplication that do not reorder accepted rows, plus a snapshot-rejection or live-version replacement rule for changed payloads with the same ID and changed sort fields

Tests where page two arrives before page one, an earlier or opposite-direction page arrives late, the same page arrives twice with identical, changed non-sort, and changed sort payloads, and a response completes after reset or reconnect
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not append a page merely because its transport request succeeded; a response that is duplicate, reversed, out of order, cyclic, or stale for the current viewer must not mutate visible state.

steps.action: Increment the request generation and reset pages and continuations when filters, search text, sort, authorization scope, reconnect, or a new viewer instance changes the query. On reopen, either start a fresh generation or validate an intentionally resumable token before use. When data shrinks, reset or refresh a cursor view, or clamp a numbered view against refreshed snapshot totals so it cannot loop on an empty out-of-range page. Limit in-flight requests, queued pages, retained rows, and prefetch distance; pause on failure and stop at explicit exhaustion.
evidence: Reset and resume rules for query change, permission change, reopen, reconnect, revision invalidation, and stale cursor outcomes
A data-shrink rule that reaches a valid final page or an explicit empty state without repeatedly requesting the same empty page
Explicit per-view bounds for in-flight requests, queued pages, retained rows, retries, and prefetch distance
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not reuse a continuation across a changed query or viewer generation, auto-fetch until the complete collection is resident, or retry a failed or nonadvancing page without a bound and state transition.

steps.action: Test empty data, one row, exactly one page, one row beyond a page, tied sort values, insertion and deletion around the cursor, deletion of the last page, complete data shrink, duplicate delivery with identical, changed non-sort, and changed sort payloads for one stable ID, reversed and out-of-order responses, old-generation completion, cursor rejection or cycles, query reset, reopen, reconnect, retry, and bounded prefetch. Route inventory click and settlement to paper-inventory-gui-interactions, protocol framing and hostile decoding to paper-plugin-protocol-safety, connection teardown to paper-player-session-lifecycle, and runtime proof to paper-plugin-testing-evidence. Keep rendering geometry, screen-specific design, persistence flush, and business-specific page sizes outside this concern.
evidence: A deterministic boundary and mutation test matrix covering every listed transition
Separate adapter evidence that the actual data source performs bounded page retrieval
A routing statement for inventory interaction, transport, player-session, and testing guidance plus explicit exclusions for rendering, design, persistence flush, and fixed business sizing
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not approve a paged UI from a first-page happy-path test, and do not fold click handling, rendering layout, persistence flush design, or project-specific list policy into this contract.

recipes.failureMode: A list can appear paged while silently dropping records, repeatedly loading the full result set, skipping tied rows, duplicating or reversing pages, publishing stale responses into a replacement viewer, looping after data shrink, or prefetching without bounds.

recipes.title: Match Paper plugin test evidence to runtime claims
when: the request implements, reviews, or reports confidence in a Paper plugin change
a test plan must choose between pure unit tests, fakes or mocks, MockBukkit, a loaded Paper server, and manual client verification
plugin bootstrap, events, commands, scheduling, persistence, inventories, packets, resources, or lifecycle behavior could compile without working on the target server
a final answer is about to claim that a feature works, is safe, or is production-ready

steps.action: List each behavior and final claim separately, then identify the boundary that can observe it: pure domain logic, an owned adapter contract, Bukkit or Paper semantics, plugin load and registration, a real server lifecycle, or a client-visible result. Record the target Minecraft and Paper version plus high-risk transitions such as enable, reload, disconnect, duplicate callbacks, cancellation, timeout, and disable.
evidence: A claim-to-observation matrix naming the runtime boundary required for every material behavior
The exact target Minecraft and Paper version or build used by runtime evidence
A risk list covering lifecycle, concurrency, persistence, transport, and client-visible behavior that is in scope
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not choose a test library or report that the feature works until every material claim has an observable proving boundary.

steps.action: Use fast pure tests for deterministic domain rules and owned adapters, test doubles for caller-controlled contracts, MockBukkit only for Paper behavior it faithfully implements, and a loaded target-version Paper server for bootstrap and runtime semantics. Use a protocol-level oracle for packet transport and shape claims, and a real instrumented client or captured client state for rendering, audio, input, resource-pack application, and other client-observed outcomes. Combine layers when one behavior crosses boundaries; compilation proves only type compatibility.
evidence: A stated evidence layer for each claim and the limitations of that layer
A loaded-server test for plugin descriptors, dependency wiring, enable or disable behavior, and registration changes
A protocol oracle for packet transport and shape claims, plus a real instrumented client or captured client state for client-visible outcomes
An explicit unsupported or unverified note where the available harness cannot prove the behavior
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not present mocks, MockBukkit, compilation, or a server-only assertion as proof of behavior outside that layer's observable contract.

steps.action: Separate domain decisions from Bukkit and external I/O, inject owned clocks, schedulers, identifiers, repositories, and transports where practical, and assert durable outcomes instead of internal call sequences. Use isolated temporary state, bounded fake responses, deterministic task advancement, and cleanup for global registries, static state, files, ports, executors, and plugin instances.
evidence: Tests run without wall-clock sleeps, unbounded retries, live network dependencies, or order dependence
Test doubles model contracts owned by the plugin instead of inventing Paper behavior
Each test restores global, filesystem, scheduler, and plugin lifecycle state even after failure
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not replace an uncontrolled runtime dependency with a nondeterministic sleep, shared singleton, or mock of undocumented Paper internals.

steps.action: Test the success path together with expected business failures, exceptions or unavailable dependencies, duplicate and out-of-order callbacks, timeout and cancellation, disconnect, reload, and disable. For asynchronous work, control completion order and prove stale results cannot publish after the owning session or plugin generation ends. For persistence, test serialization, restart or reload, migration, and partial-write recovery at the real adapter boundary.
evidence: Assertions for every typed outcome and externally visible side effect
Controlled ordering tests for asynchronous success, failure, cancellation, stale completion, and teardown
Reload or restart evidence for persistent format and migration changes
Idempotent cleanup evidence for partial enable and repeated disable paths
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not approve a lifecycle or asynchronous change from a single immediate-success test.

steps.action: Run the smallest targeted tests that prove the changed behavior, then broaden only across shared boundaries. Report exact commands, target versions, passed and failed counts, known unrelated baselines, runtime fixtures, and remaining manual or unavailable checks. Word the conclusion no stronger than the highest evidence layer actually completed.
evidence: Exact reproducible commands and target versions for each completed evidence layer
A distinction between new failures, known baselines, skipped checks, and unavailable environments
A final claim whose scope matches the strongest completed test rather than the intended deployment
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not say tests pass, the plugin works, or the change is production-ready without naming what ran and what remains unverified.

recipes.failureMode: A green compiler or convenient mock can be mistaken for runtime proof, leaving plugin load, Paper semantics, lifecycle ordering, persistence, or client-visible behavior untested while the result is reported as working.

recipes.title: Build reproducible Fabric Client GameTest visual evidence
when: A Fabric client screen, HUD, overlay, widget, visual layer, or rendered state needs repeatable visual regression evidence.
Client GameTest screenshots must remain attributable across a case matrix, partial reruns, CI, and baseline review.
A visual suite needs to distinguish layout assertions, renderer readiness, capture, and image comparison failures instead of reporting one ambiguous screenshot failure.

steps.action: Define the complete ordered case matrix before execution. Give every case a stable semantic ID derived from named dimensions such as screen, state, viewport class, resolved GUI scale, locale, and fixture rather than array position, time, or a random value. Store those dimensions with target Minecraft, resolved Fabric stack releases and mappings, test-bundle revision, renderer, asset-revision, and environment metadata. For each case, name bounded readiness barriers for the state it needs, such as world creation, chunk rendering, asset loading, screen opening, layout completion, and deterministic animation advancement; a sleep or screenshot delay is not a readiness contract.
evidence: A versioned suite definition containing the complete ordered case list and stable case IDs
Per-case semantic dimensions and target/runtime metadata without project-specific fixed dimensions
Named readiness barriers, bounded timeouts, and deterministic state or animation controls for every case
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not capture a baseline while case identity, runtime metadata, or the condition that makes the frame ready is implicit.

steps.action: Resolve selected case IDs or an inclusive stable-ID range against the frozen suite definition and reject unknown or ambiguous endpoints. Record expected, selected, executed, passed, failed, skipped, and not-selected sets separately in the run manifest. Resume only into a fresh staging area or after reconciling prior artifacts by case ID and metadata. A selected-case or range run may report results for that selection, but it is suite-complete only when every expected case is eligible, executed, reconciled, and passed in the same declared evidence set.
evidence: The immutable expected case-ID set and the exact selected-case or range expression
Separate expected, selected, executed, passed, failed, skipped, and not-selected sets
A completeness value derived from set reconciliation rather than process exit alone
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not call a selected-case, shard, resumed range, or filtered run a passing complete suite when any expected case lacks eligible evidence.

steps.action: For every case that reaches successful capture, retain one full client frame before producing a crop, comparison, or visual-pass result. A case whose primary failure occurs before or during capture may have no frame; record that phase-aware expected absence in the manifest instead of generating an independent missing-artifact failure. Optional focused crops must be derived from the case's runtime layout bounds, intersected with and verified against the captured frame, and recorded as zero-based half-open rectangles; do not bake one fixed crop size into generic guidance. Keep the full frame as the contextual source, bind every crop to its source-frame digest and bounds, and treat an empty, clipped, out-of-frame, or stale bounds result as a capture failure rather than silently comparing a convenient region.
evidence: A full-frame artifact and digest for each case that reaches successful capture, comparison, or visual pass
A phase-aware expected-absence record for an earlier readiness or assertion, render, or capture failure
Optional runtime-derived zero-based half-open crop bounds proven to lie within the source frame
A crop artifact linked to the exact source-frame digest, bounds, viewport metadata, and case ID
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not use a crop as standalone proof, infer bounds from a stale baseline, or hide surrounding rendering failures outside the crop.

steps.action: Make compare and baseline-update explicit mutually exclusive run types. A compare run reads reviewed immutable baselines and never rewrites them. A baseline-update run writes candidate baselines and review metadata to a separate staging location, preserves prior baselines, and does not turn changed pixels into a passing comparison. Record the comparator identity and version, exact or declared bounded policy, baseline digest, actual digest, difference summary, and review disposition per case; require deliberate promotion outside the test run.
evidence: An explicit compare or baseline-update run type in command output and the run manifest
Immutable reviewed baseline, actual, and candidate digests plus comparator version and policy
A human-reviewable difference and deliberate promotion record for every candidate baseline
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not overwrite a reviewed baseline during comparison or report baseline generation as a successful visual assertion.

steps.action: Write artifacts to a run-scoped staging directory, finalize them only after digesting and manifesting them, and clean run-owned temporary state in a finally-equivalent path. Derive each case's expected artifact roles from its primary phase: require a full frame when capture succeeded, but record an expected absence when readiness or assertion, render, or capture failed first. Before reporting, reconcile the manifest against those phase-aware expectations and the expected and selected sets, then fail on a manifest-expected missing artifact, stale metadata, duplicates, or unexpected artifacts. Make cleanup idempotent so an interrupted run can be retried without inheriting evidence. Classify the primary result for each case as readiness or assertion, render, capture, compare, or infrastructure failure, preserve secondary diagnostics, and never replace the first causal phase with a later missing-file error.
evidence: A run-scoped artifact manifest with case IDs, primary phases, expected or absent artifact roles, metadata digests, paths or logical names, byte sizes, and content digests
Reconciliation results for missing, stale, duplicate, and unexpected artifacts
Repeat-run evidence that cleanup is bounded, ownership-aware, and idempotent
Per-case primary failure phase plus preserved secondary diagnostics
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not publish a green run while the artifact directory contains unowned files, an expected artifact is missing, metadata is stale, or the failure phase is ambiguous.

steps.action: Label whether evidence came from deterministic non-render assertions, a Fabric Client GameTest client under a virtual framebuffer, or an interactive client environment. A virtual-framebuffer run can exercise an actual client render-and-capture path in that declared environment, but it does not prove physical display, GPU and driver, window-manager, native input, accessibility, shader, or complete installed-extension-set behavior. Non-client headless assertions prove no rendered pixels. Interactive-client evidence is still specific to its recorded environment. Verify every concrete test entrypoint, screenshot, wait, and Loom configuration name against current official Fabric documentation and target-version Fabric API or mapping documentation instead of presenting one API spelling as universal.
evidence: An environment class and recorded client, operating system, display, renderer, hardware or software graphics, window, GUI scale, locale, and relevant client-extension metadata
https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/automatic-testing
https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/loom/fabric-api
Target-version Fabric API Javadocs or selected mappings for every concrete client-test API named by an implementation
A limitations statement distinguishing non-render assertions, virtual-framebuffer client evidence, and interactive-client evidence
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not describe non-client assertions as rendered evidence, virtual-framebuffer results as hardware or interaction proof, or target-specific Fabric API names as universal.

recipes.failureMode: Screenshots can look authoritative while unstable case identity, early capture, partial selection, silent baseline replacement, stale artifacts, or an overstated headless environment makes the evidence incomplete or irreproducible.

recipes.title: Design Fabric client UI without double scaling or hidden clipping
when: The task creates or reviews a Fabric client screen, overlay, widget, or custom UI layout.
Text, images, controls, or input regions clip, shift, shrink, or stop aligning when GUI scale, window size, language, or interaction state changes.
The UI needs repeatable geometry and rendered evidence across multiple client display conditions.

steps.action: Read the target-version screen or window values that already represent the current scaled viewport and establish them as the layout coordinate space. Capture configured GUI scale, resolved scale, window and framebuffer dimensions, and scaled viewport dimensions as one case tuple. Treat Auto as a runtime-resolved family of tuples, not as one magic scale value. Do not apply GUI scale again to layout, draw, clip, or pointer coordinates.
evidence: A coordinate-space table for viewport, framebuffer, draw, clip, and input values
Captured case tuples including configured GUI scale, resolved scale, window dimensions, framebuffer dimensions, and scaled viewport dimensions
Current official Fabric documentation and target-version mappings for concrete Screen and window APIs
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not compensate for uncertain coordinates with another scale multiplication or division; verify the target-version scaled viewport and input surfaces first.

steps.action: Compute an immutable layout result from the scaled viewport, content measurements, and interaction state. Include component bounds, pre-clip content bounds, child placement, local clip, parent clip, effective ancestor intersection, and hit-test or focus bounds. Consume this same result for rendering, clip setup, and input instead of rebuilding related rectangles in separate paths.
evidence: One layout-result type or fixture containing every render, clip, child, and hit-test rectangle
Assertions that component and ancestor clips form the effective intersection
Assertions that render and input paths consume the same state-specific layout result
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not approve separately calculated draw, scissor, and pointer bounds whose equality is only assumed.

steps.action: Measure complete glyph and image bounds before applying clips. Compare those bounds with the component, parent, and effective clip. If content intentionally exceeds a boundary, select and test an explicit wrapping, scrolling, ellipsis, crop, or overflow policy; clipped output alone must not turn accidental overflow into a passing result. Keep nested clip ownership balanced on every render path.
evidence: Pre-clip glyph and image rectangles
Component, parent, and effective clip comparisons
An explicit and tested overflow policy for every intentionally non-fitting content path
Balanced nested clip setup and teardown across normal and exceptional render paths
steps.stopIfMissing: A clean post-clip screenshot is not evidence that full content bounds fit or that nested clips are balanced.

steps.action: Define a deterministic case matrix with the minimum supported scaled viewport, long localized translations, multiple resolved scales, Auto at more than one window size, and normal, hover, pressed, and disabled states. Assert layout bounds, pre-clip content, clip intersections, and hit regions for every case. Then capture actual client renders or screenshots for the same matrix so visual artifacts supplement rather than replace geometry proof.
evidence: Parameterized geometry tests for every viewport, scale, Auto, translation, and interaction-state case
Numeric assertions for layout, pre-clip content, effective clips, and hit-test bounds
Actual-render or screenshot artifacts labeled with the same case tuples
A review result that distinguishes deterministic geometry failures from visual-rendering failures
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not claim scale or clipping safety from the default language, one large viewport, one GUI scale, one interaction state, or screenshots alone.

steps.action: Consult current official Fabric custom-screen and GUI-rendering documentation plus target-version mappings to verify every concrete Screen, window, drawing, input, and scissor API named by the implementation. Keep unverified details out of generated code and present the coordinate, layout, and test rules as general design guidance when exact APIs are unavailable.
evidence: https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/rendering/gui/custom-screens
https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/rendering/gui-graphics
Target-version Fabric Yarn or other selected mapping documentation for each named Minecraft API
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not convert general UI geometry guidance into target-version API claims without current official documentation and mapping evidence.

recipes.failureMode: Independent scale, render, clip, and input calculations can pass a single screenshot while producing clipped content or misaligned controls in other resolved viewport cases.

recipes.title: Generate or review bounded Paper world operations across chunk boundaries
when: the request loads, generates, pins, scans, or mutates multiple chunks from a Paper or Bukkit plugin
block edits, drops, entity movement or removal, or teleportation can cross a chunk, tick, unload, or Folia region boundary
the implementation uses async chunk loading, plugin chunk tickets, repeated world batches, RegionScheduler, EntityScheduler, or chunk lifecycle events
the review must prevent tick-thread blocking, stale references, ticket leaks, duplicate partial side effects, or shutdown races

steps.action: Resolve the target Paper version and verify the exact World, Chunk, Block, Entity, teleport, RegionScheduler, EntityScheduler, and event APIs from official Paper sources. Convert the complete requested selection into deduplicated world-and-chunk coordinates, define generation allowed or forbidden, and reject unknown, unbounded, or over-limit work before loading or mutation begins.
evidence: Target-version Javadocs matches for every overload and callback or completion context used
A bounded target manifest containing world identities, chunk coordinates, generation policy, maximum chunks, maximum targets, timeout, and rejection rules
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not begin loading or mutation until the complete chunk set, generation policy, target-version APIs, and hard limits are known.

steps.action: Acquire only the bounded target chunks through target-version-supported asynchronous APIs. Never wait or block via Future.get or Future.join on a server main, tick, or region thread. Treat isChunkLoaded as a snapshot, and if residency is required, let one lifecycle owner track exact plugin-ticket claims, shared references, deadlines, and release responsibility.
evidence: Target-version evidence for async chunk acquisition, generation flags, callback or Future completion context, isChunkLoaded, and plugin-ticket add and remove behavior
A bounded acquisition queue and ticket ledger that distinguishes claims added by this operation from same-plugin shared residency
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not synchronously wait on chunk acquisition or treat a loaded snapshot as a lease; reject the design until asynchronous continuation and owned residency are explicit.

steps.action: Never dereference a retained world target outside its verified owner or treat it as current after lifecycle changes without owner-local revalidation. Carry immutable world identity plus coordinates for block and location work, then re-resolve and validate them on the owning region. For entity work, use that entity's scheduler as the handoff mechanism and validate the entity's identity, validity, lifecycle state, operation generation, plugin state, and preconditions inside the owned callback instead of requiring a cross-region World.getEntity lookup. Keep EntityScheduler retired callbacks minimal: record or forward terminal intent only, then perform entity, chunk, world, or ticket cleanup in a verified safe context.
evidence: A scheduler-ownership map for Paper and any claimed Folia support

Tests proving retained Chunk, Block, BlockState, mutable Location, and Entity values are never dereferenced outside their verified owner or treated as current after lifecycle changes without owner-local revalidation
An entity-scheduler handoff that revalidates the entity inside the owned callback without requiring cross-region World.getEntity lookup, plus a location-region path for block and location mutation
A retired or scheduling-failure path whose critical retired callback only records or forwards minimal terminal intent and defers entity, chunk, world, and ticket-level cleanup
steps.stopIfMissing: Async completion is not mutation ownership; do not touch block or location state until it is re-resolved in its owning region, or entity state until the entity-scheduler callback revalidates it.

steps.action: Process a fixed maximum of targets and elapsed work per tick and per region, recording a resumable cursor and bounded diagnostics. Stop when cancelled, timed out, stale, unloaded, or disabled, and emit complete, partial, rejected, timeout, stale, or unloaded with attempted, applied, skipped, failed, and remaining counts.
evidence: Explicit item and time budgets for each tick and region plus an upper bound on queued callbacks and diagnostics
Typed progress and terminal outcomes that do not equate Future or callback completion with full mutation success
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not run an unbounded chunk, block, drop, or entity loop in one callback or report unconditional success without per-target progress.

steps.action: Before every side effect and resumed batch, recheck assumptions affected by neighboring physics, drops, entity movement or removal, teleport completion, chunk unload, cancellation, and plugin disable. Inspect teleport Boolean results, treat entity retirement or unload separately from death or despawn, and never use applyPhysics=false as a general safety or persistence guarantee.
evidence: Target-version Paper Javadocs for block physics flags, teleport results, entity scheduler retirement, and chunk or entity lifecycle events used
Race tests in which physics changes neighbors, a dropped or moved entity disappears, teleport returns false, a chunk unloads, or plugin disable begins between acquisition and apply
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not infer a final world state from scheduling, event delivery, applyPhysics=false, an unloaded entity, or a completed teleport Future; inspect the actual result and current target.

steps.action: Give the operation a stable identity and record per-target compare-before-apply progress. On retry or recovery, reconcile observed postconditions and resume only unapplied work so drops, entity removals, teleports, and other non-idempotent effects cannot repeat after partial completion.
evidence: A per-target progress model and compare-before-apply rule
Tests that interrupt after partial mutation and prove retries neither repeat committed side effects nor skip remaining work
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not retry a partially applied world operation until committed effects can be distinguished from remaining work.

steps.action: Use one lifecycle owner to accept exactly one terminal transition, stop new work, reconcile committed effects, settle the typed outcome, and release every owned ticket or scheduled resource once. Cover complete, partial, rejected, timeout, stale, unloaded, cancellation, exception, and plugin disable independently of whether lifecycle events arrive.
evidence: A ticket ledger and terminal-state transition that release only owned claims and handle shared same-plugin residency
Assertions that every terminal and plugin-disable path leaves no operation-owned tickets, batches, or unresolved completion
Tests proving duplicate events, callbacks, cancellation, and shutdown cleanup are idempotent
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not rely on automatic ticket release or events alone; the lifecycle owner must independently release every owned claim exactly once.

recipes.failureMode: A cross-chunk operation can block the owning tick, pin unbounded chunks, cross scheduler ownership, reuse unloaded targets, repeat partial side effects, or leak resources unless target discovery, acquisition, batches, outcomes, reconciliation, and cleanup share one bounded lifecycle.

recipes.title: Generate or review lifecycle-safe Paper custom recipes
when: the request adds shaped or shapeless recipes from code or configuration
recipe definitions can change while the plugin or server remains running
custom ItemStack metadata determines which ingredients are valid
online players must receive or discover recipes registered after enable
the request diagnoses duplicate keys, stale recipes, false registration results, or recipe-book visibility

steps.action: Resolve the target Paper version and verify every referenced recipe, key, ingredient-choice, registration, removal, and player-discovery type or member against target-version Paper Javadocs. Read the official recipe behavior documentation before deciding when registration and client resends occur.
evidence: Target-version matches for NamespacedKey, recipe types, RecipeChoice variants, addRecipe, removeRecipe, and any discovery methods used
Official Paper recipe documentation for registration timing and client resends
An explicit runtime context for every global recipe-registry mutation
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not invent recipe overloads, ingredient semantics, discovery behavior, or a safe mutation context from type names alone.

steps.action: Give every recipe a stable plugin-owned NamespacedKey and declare whether each ingredient uses material identity, exact stack identity, or a separately verified custom matching flow. RecipeChoice.ExactChoice matches the complete stack aside from amount; use it only when that is the intended contract, and do not weaken an unrepresentable custom identity to material-only matching.
evidence: A stable key and owning plugin for every desired recipe
An ingredient-identity matrix naming material, exact-stack, or custom-flow semantics per slot
Positive and negative matching examples including amount and metadata differences
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not register a recipe until key ownership and ingredient identity are unambiguous.

steps.action: Validate keys, results, shaped patterns, ingredient symbols, and shapeless counts against target-version recipe contracts before mutation. Build canonical match signatures for the desired plugin-owned set: shaped signatures preserve normalized occupied bounds, slot positions, and ingredient identity while including only target-verified symmetry behavior; shapeless signatures use a counted multiset of ingredient identities. Reject duplicate keys and report distinct recipes whose signatures can match the same crafting input, even when their outputs differ.
evidence: A fully validated desired definition set with no duplicate NamespacedKeys
Canonical shaped and shapeless match signatures derived from the declared ingredient-identity contract
A collision report covering equal inputs with equal or different outputs
Target-version evidence for any assumed mirroring, symmetry, tag, or choice behavior
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not choose a winner by declaration order or assume rotations, mirroring, tags, or custom-choice behavior that target-version evidence does not establish.

steps.action: Parse and validate all desired definitions before mutation, diff them against the last applied plugin-owned key set, and reconcile unchanged, added, changed, and removed recipes without clearing or resetting the global recipe registry. Observe every addRecipe and removeRecipe result, record partial progress, and recover toward the last-known-good owned definitions when replacement fails.
evidence: A staged desired definition set and an owned-key diff
Typed outcomes for added, unchanged, replaced, removed, rejected, restored, and partially reconciled recipes
Per-key add and remove results plus recovery and observability for partial failure
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not report reload success after an ignored false result, partial mutation, global clearRecipes, or resetRecipes.

steps.action: Define recipe-list resend and recipe-book discovery as separate policies. Use target-version resend controls when online clients must observe late additions or removals, and use discover or undiscover operations only when the product requires recipe-book state. Test enable, unchanged reload, add, change, remove, duplicate or conflicting key, equal-input collision, partial failure, disable, re-enable, online-player visibility, discovery retention, ingredient mismatches, consumption, and output on a loaded target-version server and client where visibility is claimed.
evidence: A separate resend policy and recipe-book discovery policy
Loaded-server results for registry reconciliation, matching, consumption, output, reload, disable, and re-enable
Client evidence for late recipe-list visibility and recipe-book behavior when those outcomes are claimed
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not treat successful server registration as proof that an online client received or discovered the recipe.

recipes.failureMode: Custom recipes can overwrite unrelated registry entries, disappear or duplicate across reload, match the wrong items, leave clients stale, or report success after a partial global mutation.

recipes.title: Design aligned and owned Paper display interaction surfaces
when: the request pairs TextDisplay, ItemDisplay, or BlockDisplay entities with Interaction entities
a hologram, world-space control, board, label, or other display-backed surface must be clickable
the visible content and Interaction hitbox are offset, rotated differently, intermittently clickable, or stale after refresh
display and hit-target entities can leak, duplicate, or survive a reload with ambiguous ownership
client-side display interpolation or billboard behavior can diverge from the server-side interaction target

steps.action: Resolve the target Paper version and verify every Display subtype, Interaction member, entity lifecycle member, and interaction event actually used against the matching Paper API surface and current official behavior documentation. The official display guide says display entities were added in 1.19.4, marks the page fully accurate from 1.20, describes displays as having no hitbox by default, and distinguishes the centered ItemDisplay model origin from the BlockDisplay corner origin. Treat those statements as version-scoped behavior evidence and treat bundled type/member indexes as name evidence only. The current Display Javadocs describe a visual-only entity, while Interaction is a separate entity that records interactions and exposes its own width, height, and response settings.
evidence: Target-version matches for Display, the selected TextDisplay, ItemDisplay, or BlockDisplay subtype, Interaction, every transformation or dimension member used, and the selected interaction event
Official display behavior and origin guidance: https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/display-entities/
Matching target-version Display and Interaction Javadocs selected from https://jd.papermc.io/paper/ rather than a fixed latest-version route
An explicit list of visual, hit-target, persistence, visibility, scheduler, and event assumptions not established by type/member indexes
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not invent an older-version Display or Interaction API, infer hitbox geometry from similar method names, or copy latest-version event and transformation behavior into an unresolved target.

steps.action: Define one immutable local-space layout contract before spawning entities: surface anchor, horizontal and vertical axes, forward direction, units, logical element rectangles, depth ordering, display subtype and model origin, transformation order, and the conversion from each logical rectangle to both its visual pose and Interaction location, width, and height. Keep Display transformation, billboard, display width or height, view range, and client interpolation distinct from Interaction dimensions; no similarly named Display value proves a clickable bound. Account for ItemDisplay center versus BlockDisplay corner origins, and verify TextDisplay or custom-model pivots in the target client instead of guessing. Derive both entity specifications from the same pure layout result so configuration defaults, runtime overrides, refreshes, and tests cannot apply competing offsets.
evidence: A coordinate contract naming anchor, axes, units, facing, subtype origin, transformation order, and every configurable offset exactly once
A pure layout model whose element ID produces the display specification and Interaction specification together
Boundary examples for minimum and maximum element positions, rotations, scales, and hit-target sizes
Target-client evidence for subtype or resource-pack model pivots and any billboarded or transformed clickable surface
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not maintain a display-position formula beside an unrelated hitbox-position formula, reuse Display width or height as Interaction bounds without proof, or assume a billboard, affine transform, or custom model also rotates and scales the server interaction target.

steps.action: Give every logical surface and element stable plugin-owned identities, a generation, and explicit display or hit-target roles. Build replacement specifications and a pending registry record before spawning any hit target. Choose and prove a staging mechanism that keeps every pending Interaction outside live input space until its entity identity is registered and the complete generation can be published in one serialized, non-suspending owner-context transition. Never place an unregistered or pending Interaction at a live hit location; if the platform boundary cannot make exposure atomic, keep the previous generation authoritative and the replacement hit targets unavailable until the publication fence can complete. Remove partial creations on failure, then retire only the previous owned generation after the replacement is current. Define whether entities are temporary or durable, how reload or restart rediscovers durable ownership, and how missing, duplicated, mismatched, or foreign entities are handled. The official display guide warns that setPersistent(false) does not remove a temporary display from a chunk that never unloads, so always execute explicit idempotent removal. Keep lookups and reconciliation bounded by owned IDs or indexed locations; do not scan or delete every Display or Interaction in a world, and route storage, scheduler, and cross-chunk mechanics to their dedicated guidance.
evidence: An ownership record for surface ID, element ID, generation, display entity, Interaction entity, persistence policy, and authoritative registry
A staged create, input-unavailable, register, publish, retire, and rollback transition with no live pending Interaction and idempotent removal of both roles
A bounded reconciliation table for complete pair, missing display, missing hit target, duplicates, stale generation, malformed ownership, and foreign entity
Reload, disable, partial-spawn failure, repeated refresh, and never-unloading-chunk tests with balanced created and removed entity counts
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not delete entities by type, custom name, proximity, or display content; place an unregistered or pending Interaction in live input space; publish half a pair; retain an old generation after replacement; or rely on chunk unload as the cleanup path.

steps.action: Resolve an event's clicked Interaction through the current owned generation to one logical element before running domain actions. Define right-click versus attack scope, intended hand, cancellation policy, permissions, viewer or session eligibility, and exactly-once behavior. Treat PlayerInteractEntityEvent as the parent right-click candidate and PlayerInteractAtEntityEvent as the position-specific candidate, then verify the matching target-version Javadocs for their hand, cancellation, position, and delivery semantics. When the target-version position-specific Javadocs warn that the client can send it spuriously in addition to the parent event, follow their recommendation to use the parent unless the position is required. Choose one verified event path or an explicit deduplication rule rather than executing both. Delegate listener priority, cancellation interoperability, thread context, and deferred side effects to the general Paper event-listener contract.
evidence: The target-version event class, clicked entity accessor, hand accessor, cancellation behavior, and clicked-position accessor only when position is required
Matching target-version PlayerInteractEntityEvent Javadocs selected from https://jd.papermc.io/paper/
Matching target-version PlayerInteractAtEntityEvent Javadocs and any duplicate-delivery warning selected from https://jd.papermc.io/paper/
Tests for main hand, off hand, cancelled event, stale generation, foreign Interaction, repeated event delivery, unauthorized viewer, and missing logical element
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not execute once per hand, listen to both parent and position-specific events without a duplicate policy, trust any Interaction entity of the right type, or treat a stale entity reference as a current logical element.

steps.action: Test the pure layout first with exact vectors, rectangles, pivots, rotations, and generated pair specifications. Then load the plugin on the target Paper version to verify spawn, registry publication, interaction mapping, replacement, rollback, reload, disable, and bounded cleanup. Use a real target client or captured client state for visible alignment, custom-model pivots, billboard behavior, view range, and interpolation because server entity state cannot prove the rendered pose. Inspect debug hitboxes where applicable and click the visual center and boundaries from representative approach angles. For a moving display, define when the surface is clickable and test that policy instead of assuming client-side interpolation keeps the server Interaction synchronized.
evidence: Pure deterministic layout tests covering subtype origins, configuration overrides, boundary positions, transformations, and paired entity specifications
Loaded target-version Paper tests for complete and partial spawn, current-generation event routing, repeated refresh, reload reconciliation, disable, and foreign-entity preservation
Target-client screenshots or captured state with visible content and debug hitboxes, plus center, edge, outside, hand, and approach-angle interaction results
A leak assertion showing bounded registry size and balanced owned Display and Interaction creation or removal across repeated lifecycle transitions
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not claim visual alignment from pure matrices or server locations alone, claim click correctness from a synthetic event alone, or claim cleanup from one successful disable without partial and repeated lifecycle cases.

recipes.failureMode: A display-backed control can look correct while its independent Interaction target is offset or stale, execute twice, leak generations, or delete another plugin's entities when geometry and ownership are not one explicit contract.

recipes.title: Bound high-frequency Paper persistence under contention
when: a Paper event, task, command, or callback can produce database mutations repeatedly or in bursts
multiple plugin instances, workers, or callbacks can contend on the same durable key or transaction
the implementation considers direct atomic writes, write-behind batching, or per-key delta coalescing
serialization failures, deadlocks, ambiguous commits, partial flushes, queue growth, shutdown durability, or lost updates are possible
the request claims database contention safety or retry correctness

steps.action: Inventory every persistence producer before choosing a write path. Record steady and peak events per second, burst duration, active and maximum key cardinality, approximate bytes per pending entry, acceptable durability-loss window, required visibility latency, and ordering or conflict semantics. Classify each mutation as an atomic state transition, mergeable delta, latest-value replacement, ordered append, set-like merge, or external side effect; state whether it is associative, commutative, idempotent, and safe to replay.
evidence: A producer matrix with measured or explicitly bounded steady rate, peak rate, burst duration, key cardinality, and pending bytes
A durability and visibility budget for each producer, including the maximum acknowledged-but-not-durable window
An ordering and algebra table showing which values can be combined, reordered, replayed, or deduplicated
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not select per-event writes, batching, or coalescing from intuition alone when event rate, key growth, durability, or ordering requirements are unknown.

steps.action: Use a database-side atomic mutation or compare-and-set style transition when each event must become durable promptly, the operation has strict order or preconditions, or measured contention is acceptable. Use bounded per-key delta coalescing only for deltas whose combination is proven associative and commutative under the domain's overflow and range rules. Define the coalescing key, accumulator type, flush trigger, maximum age, maximum keys, maximum bytes, maximum delta magnitude, and admission result. Keep ordered appends, state-machine transitions, latest-value updates, and non-idempotent effects on paths that preserve their distinct semantics instead of forcing them into a delta accumulator.
evidence: A decision for each producer between direct atomic mutation and bounded per-key coalescing, tied to the rate and durability matrix
Database-adapter evidence that the direct mutation is atomic under the claimed isolation and conflict model
Property or table-driven tests proving the selected delta merge law, range behavior, and equivalence to the accepted event sequence
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not coalesce a mutation whose result depends on event order, an intermediate state, a read-time precondition, or a non-idempotent side effect.

steps.action: Capture immutable plugin-owned input in the event context, then perform connection acquisition, statements, commits, rollbacks, retries, and journal I/O off the Paper server or region tick context. Publish any Bukkit-facing result only through the target-version-compatible execution context after revalidating the target. Bound pending keys, estimated bytes, oldest age, in-flight flushes, retry attempts, and total retry time. Define explicit non-blocking admission outcomes such as accepted, coalesced, deferred to a bounded durable journal, rejected, or degraded; never turn a full queue into an unbounded map, a silent durable-data drop, or a database wait on the server thread.
evidence: Target-version Paper scheduling documentation for every tick-context capture and Bukkit-facing publication boundary
Configured and tested limits for pending keys, approximate bytes, oldest age, concurrent flushes, retry attempts, and retry deadline
A backpressure table stating the caller-visible outcome and durability implication at each limit
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not execute database work or wait for queue capacity in a Paper event or tick context, and do not describe a queue as bounded without key, memory, age, and in-flight limits.

steps.action: Flush an immutable snapshot with a stable batch identity while new events accumulate separately. Track the exact accepted amount, the exact durable amount, and the exact uncommitted remainder for every key. After a known rollback or per-key partial result, merge only the uncommitted remainder back into the live accumulator atomically with concurrently accepted deltas. After an unknown commit outcome, reconcile through an idempotency key, durable batch ledger, revision, or adapter-supported outcome check before reapplying; never blindly requeue the whole snapshot. Cap requeue age and attempts, preserve the original durability budget, and surface terminal recovery work instead of losing or double-applying it.
evidence: A per-key accounting invariant showing accepted equals durable plus live pending plus explicit terminal or rejected outcomes
Tests for full success, known rollback, a partial per-key flush, failure while new deltas arrive, duplicate acknowledgement, and unknown commit outcome
An idempotency, revision, or durable batch-ledger design that prevents ambiguous requeue from applying a snapshot twice
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not clear live accumulators before snapshot ownership is recorded, requeue already durable entries, or retry an unknown commit outcome without reconciliation or idempotency.

steps.action: Classify a retryable serialization or deadlock conflict only from the actual database and driver contract, including documented typed exceptions, codes, cause chains, and transaction state. Do not infer retryability from generic transient categories or message text. On a verified retryable conflict, roll back and discard the failed transaction, start a fresh whole transaction, reacquire current state, and rerun every statement in the unit with bounded attempts, jitter, and an overall deadline. Propagate constraint violations, connectivity failures, timeouts, cancellation, unknown commit outcomes, and unclassified failures to their explicit recovery paths unless the selected adapter documents otherwise. Keep messages, commands, HTTP calls, item grants, and other external side effects outside the retryable transaction; publish them after a known commit or through an idempotent outbox-style boundary.
evidence: Official database and driver documentation plus real-adapter tests for every exception, code, and cause-chain classified as retryable
A transaction wrapper test proving rollback, fresh transaction state, complete unit replay, attempt and deadline limits, and cancellation propagation
A side-effect ledger showing that retrying a transaction cannot repeat a player-visible, network, command, or item-delivery effect
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not retry one failed statement inside a damaged transaction, retry every SQLException, parse localized messages, or run non-idempotent external side effects inside a retryable unit.

steps.action: Define a lifecycle state that closes admission before shutdown, stops periodic scheduling, waits behind a bounded in-flight barrier, performs only host-permitted final flush work, and then closes executors, journals, and database resources in dependency order. If the durability budget cannot be met, persist a bounded recovery journal or expose an explicit undurable remainder and restart reconciliation contract. Observe accepted, coalesced, deferred, rejected, and terminal events; pending keys and estimated bytes; oldest age; flush size, latency, and failures; retry classification and attempt; saturation duration; ambiguous commits; recovery lag; and shutdown outcome without logging sensitive payloads or unbounded key labels.
evidence: A bounded stop sequence with admission closure, scheduler stop, in-flight barrier, final flush or recovery handoff, and dependency-ordered close
Restart tests for a clean shutdown, deadline expiry, interrupted flush, recovery replay, and an ambiguous prior commit
Metrics or structured logs for rate, bounds, age, flushes, classified retries, saturation, recovery, and shutdown with controlled cardinality and redaction
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not start fire-and-forget database work after disable, wait without a deadline, silently discard an undurable remainder, or expose raw keys and values as metric labels.

steps.action: Use controlled clocks, retry-delay sources, executors, barriers, and scripted adapter outcomes to deterministically exercise interleavings without sleeps. Also run contention tests against the real database adapter and driver used by the project so the claimed isolation, atomic mutation, rollback exception classification, ambiguous-commit handling, and retry behavior are observed rather than mocked. Record adapter and isolation configuration, concurrent writer count, repetitions, invariant checks, failures, and limitations. When pending writes, tasks, callbacks, or cleanup are owned by a player connection, route connection generations, stale publication, reconnect, quit, and teardown to the existing paper-player-session-lifecycle recipe instead of duplicating session ownership rules here.
evidence: Deterministic tests for writer interleavings, backpressure, flush races, partial results, retry jitter and deadlines, shutdown, and recovery using controlled time, retry delays, and execution
Real-adapter contention evidence for every atomicity, isolation, conflict-classification, and whole-transaction retry claim
A scope statement routing player-connection ownership and teardown to paper-player-session-lifecycle
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not cite a memory fake as proof of database contention behavior, use wall-clock sleeps as ordering evidence, or reimplement player-session cleanup inside this persistence concern.

recipes.failureMode: Unmeasured per-event writes or unbounded coalescing can stall the server thread, exhaust memory, lose or duplicate partial flushes, replay unsafe side effects, amplify contention, and report durability that shutdown and real-adapter tests do not prove.

recipes.title: Reconcile Paper attribute modifiers and potion effects by explicit ownership
when: the request adds or refreshes equipment AttributeModifier entries through ItemMeta
a Paper plugin applies session AttributeInstance modifiers or PotionEffect values from one or more sources
attribute or effect state is rebuilt after reapply, expiry, death, quit, reconnect, plugin reload, or disable
maximum health or maximum absorption changes can make a current value exceed its new capacity
the request investigates duplicated modifiers, hidden weaker effects, lost vanilla equipment behavior, or foreign state removed during cleanup

steps.action: Resolve the target Paper version and verify the exact types and members used for AttributeModifier, AttributeInstance, Attribute, ItemMeta, ItemType, PotionEffect, PotionEffectType, LivingEntity, and Damageable. Read the target-version Javadocs for behavior that an index cannot prove. For Paper 1.21.11 after that exact verification, attribute modifiers are keyed, AttributeInstance has key-based lookup and removal plus transient modifiers, ItemMeta exposes copied modifier collections, and PotionEffect identifies a type and an active or hidden chain but has no plugin-owner key. Treat each statement as target-version evidence rather than a cross-version assumption.
evidence: Target-version type and member matches for every attribute, item-meta, potion-effect, and current-value API named in generated code
Primary Javadocs evidence for modifier key identity, transient persistence, ItemMeta default override behavior, potion active and hidden chains, and current-value bounds
An explicit list of runtime semantics that still require a loaded target-version Paper test
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not substitute deprecated UUID or name constructors, infer potion-effect ownership from a type key, or guess replacement and persistence behavior from member names.

steps.action: Represent every contribution with a stable logical source identifier, lifetime, target surface, attribute or effect type, and the verified fields needed by that surface. Derive the complete desired contribution set from authoritative equipment and session state on every reconciliation; do not treat the entity's current modifiers or effects as the source of truth. Assign each owned attribute contribution a stable NamespacedKey based on logical source, attribute, surface, and slot grouping where relevant. Keep a bounded registry of current and retired owned keys so reload or migration can remove stale owned entries without claiming an entire namespace. Fold multiple plugin sources for the same potion-effect type into one deterministic desired result and declare tie, expiry, and collision policy without embedding combat-balance values in the ownership layer.
evidence: A source-to-surface table covering equipment metadata, session attributes, and potion-effect types
A deterministic current-and-retired key registry for all plugin-owned attribute contributions
A pure aggregation table for multiple sources, equal priority, weaker reapply, expiry, and empty desired state
An explicit separation between ownership mechanics and configurable balance amounts or durations
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not generate a random key or UUID on each apply, append one modifier or effect per callback, or reconstruct desired state by copying whatever happens to be active.

steps.action: For equipment-owned contributions, read ItemMeta modifier copies, partition exact known plugin-owned keys from foreign entries, replace only owned entries, and publish the rebuilt metadata through the target-version ItemStack contract. Avoid attribute-wide, slot-wide, and whole-map removal unless the plugin explicitly owns that complete scope. Account for the distinction between absent custom metadata and an explicit empty modifier map: custom ItemMeta modifiers can override ItemType default attribute modifiers. When the final owned override disappears, return to the unset representation only when authoritative equipment state proves the plugin introduced that override; otherwise preserve the observed representation and report ambiguity. When foreign explicit entries remain, preserve them. Verify the effective equipped result, including vanilla defaults, rather than comparing only the explicit metadata map. Logical ItemStack identity, item migration, and persistent-data schema are separate concerns.
evidence: A before-and-after partition of known owned keys, foreign explicit modifiers, and implicit ItemType defaults
Idempotence tests for repeated rebuild and removal of the final owned entry
A loaded-server equipment test proving effective vanilla defaults and foreign modifiers survive
A scope statement excluding logical ItemStack identity, item migration, and persistent-data schema
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not call broad ItemMeta modifier clearing or assume preserving the explicit map automatically preserves implicit vanilla equipment behavior.

steps.action: For session contributions, compare the authoritative desired keyed set with AttributeInstance modifier copies. Remove stale or changed entries only by exact plugin-owned key, preserve vanilla and foreign keys, and add the desired replacement once. Use transient modifiers for session-only state when the verified target API and lifecycle require non-persistence, and do not rewrite the attribute base value to emulate an owned modifier. Reconcile on apply, source change, expiry, death policy, quit, reconnect, reload, and disable so repeated signals converge to the same result and an old session cannot stack into a replacement session.
evidence: A three-way desired, existing-owned, and existing-foreign reconciliation table
Tests for multiple sources, same-key replacement, stale-key removal, foreign preservation, deterministic ordering, and repeated application
Lifecycle tests for expiry, death, quit, reconnect, reload, disable, and duplicate cleanup signals
Loaded-server evidence that transient session modifiers have the intended save and reconnect behavior
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not clear an AttributeInstance, mutate its base value, or remove a modifier whose exact stable key is outside the plugin's ownership registry.

steps.action: Treat PotionEffectType as a collision domain, not an owner identity: PotionEffect has no per-source NamespacedKey, and another plugin or vanilla mechanic can produce an indistinguishable effect. Aggregate plugin sources to at most one desired contribution per type. By default, preserve an unexpected active or hidden chain and skip, reject, or choose a separately owned mechanic instead of claiming it. Only replace or remove a type under a documented exclusive type lease, and relinquish that lease when the observed chain no longer matches the plugin-controlled state. Because LivingEntity removal is type-wide, never use it as generic owned cleanup. Check add results and inspect the resulting active and hidden chain; specifically test weaker reapply so repeated refresh cannot accumulate hidden effects. Use bounded durations or another explicit recovery contract when a crash or restart loses the ownership ledger.
evidence: A collision policy for each managed effect type, including the safe action when foreign or unexpected state is present
A deterministic aggregation test for multiple plugin sources and weaker desired reapply
Target-version loaded-server observations of add return values plus active and hidden chains
Expiry, death, quit, reconnect, reload, and crash-recovery tests that never delete an unowned same-type effect
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not infer potion-effect ownership from matching type, amplifier, duration, ambient, particle, or icon fields, and do not remove by type unless exclusive ownership is both declared and still observed.

steps.action: When owned changes affect Attribute.MAX_HEALTH or Attribute.MAX_ABSORPTION on the verified target, first reconcile all capacity modifiers, then read the resulting capacity and clamp current values safely. Preserve a current value that is already within bounds, keep zero health at zero instead of resurrecting a dead entity, and reject or normalize non-finite and negative inputs before a setter can throw. Clamp health to the resulting maximum-health capacity and absorption to the resulting maximum-absorption capacity. Do not rely on undocumented automatic setter interaction, especially where target Javadocs say the effect of maximum absorption is unspecified. Exercise this ordering together with the ownership lifecycle and report loaded-server evidence separately from pure reconciliation tests.
evidence: An operation sequence that reconciles capacity before reading and clamping current health and absorption
Pure tests for raising and lowering capacity, already-valid values, zero health, negative values, and non-finite inputs
Table-driven lifecycle tests covering multiple sources, weaker reapply, expiry, death, quit, reconnect, reload, and repeated cleanup
Loaded target-version Paper evidence for modifier replacement, effective equipment defaults, potion chains, transient persistence, and capacity setter behavior
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not lower capacity after writing a now-out-of-range current value, resurrect an entity during cleanup, or report Paper runtime behavior from pure aggregation tests alone.

recipes.failureMode: Unstable keys, broad removal, implicit ItemMeta default changes, or false potion-effect ownership can stack contributions across lifecycle transitions, erase vanilla or foreign state, and leave health or absorption outside a reduced capacity.

recipes.title: Bind Model Engine models and animation channels fail-closed
when: a Paper plugin binds an existing Model Engine blueprint to an already selected carrier entity
carrier suppression, active-model attachment, animation playback, or publication order can expose a naked carrier or half-bound model
idle, locomotion, and action animations can compete, interrupt one another, or finish without a defined fallback

Model Engine reload or reimport, Paper teleport, despawn, a target-supported integration reload or disable-enable transition, or final plugin disable can leave an old active model, carrier, callback, or animation owner behind
the implementation must distinguish a missing dependency, unsupported integration version, missing identifier, rejected attachment, and cleanup failure

steps.action: Record the exact Paper build, installed Model Engine plugin artifact version and checksum or equivalent immutable identity, resolved integration artifact coordinates and immutable identity, and version-matched official API or source evidence used by the adapter. Declare supported version pairs, hard or soft dependency and load-order policy, and explicit dependency-absent, version-mismatch, and artifact-mismatch outcomes. Verify the blueprint or model identifier and every required animation identifier with exact case against the selected runtime and exported assets. If that exact generation supports aliases, record the authoritative alias-to-canonical mapping and reject missing, ambiguous, or case-mismatched input. Bundled Paper type and member indexes can verify Paper carrier surfaces only; they do not prove an external Model Engine API. Do not copy unverified class, method, event, artifact, or latest-documentation names into the contract.
evidence: An exact Paper and Model Engine compatibility row with immutable plugin and adapter artifact identities and version-matched official API or source evidence
A dependency, load-order, and compatibility outcome table covering hard or soft dependency, absent plugin, unsupported pair, artifact mismatch, and supported runtime
An exact-case inventory of blueprint, model, required animation, optional animation, and verified alias identifiers
Target-version Paper API evidence for only the carrier and lifecycle surfaces actually referenced
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not generate adapter calls or accept model and animation identifiers from memory, an unrelated Model Engine generation, or Paper-only search results.

steps.action: Model binding as an explicit generation state machine such as unavailable, carrier-prepared, attaching, attached-unpublished, current, retiring, and removed or failed. Declare whether the already selected carrier is integration-owned or borrowed and, for a borrowed carrier, snapshot only the properties this binding will change. Apply every required target-verified suppression and safety property, including silence, invisibility, or other base-entity visibility where required, before attachment. Resolve the blueprint, create and attach the active model, verify the adapter's positive attachment result and required initial state, then publish the generation to plugin behavior or viewers. An initial attach failure must leave no integration-published naked carrier or modeled-success state, detach partial model state, and either remove an integration-owned carrier or restore a borrowed carrier without deleting it. A replacement attach failure must keep the last known-good generation current when the verified adapter can stage both, or retire everything fail-closed when it cannot; it must never publish the candidate partially.
evidence: A state diagram with one atomic publication point after carrier configuration and verified attachment
An ordered trace proving configure carrier, attach model, verify attachment, then publish
Initial and replacement attach-failure tests proving partial state is cleaned and never advertised as current
A carrier ownership and property matrix plus tests proving integration-owned removal versus borrowed-property restoration
Client-visible proof that the base carrier does not leak when suppression is required
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not make the carrier discoverable, visible through plugin behavior, or successful to callers before attachment is positively verified.

steps.action: Define idle, locomotion, and action as explicit logical channels mapped to state machines, layers, or priorities that are verified for the selected Model Engine generation. Give each channel one owner, define whether higher-priority action masks or replaces locomotion and idle, and specify transitions for start, natural end, forced end, interruption, cancellation, model replacement, and stale completion. On action end, deterministically recompute the current locomotion or idle state for the same published generation. A missing required animation is an explicit binding or playback failure; never silently substitute a similarly named, default, or arbitrary animation. An optional animation may no-op or use a declared fallback only when that policy and target identifier were verified in advance.
evidence: An animation matrix naming owner, verified target channel or state machine, priority, loop policy, interruption policy, and end fallback
Deterministic tests for idle-to-move, move-to-idle, action masking, natural end, forced end, interruption, and stale completion
A required-versus-optional animation table with explicit missing outcomes and no undeclared substitution
Loaded-runtime evidence that the configured priority and end behavior matches the selected Model Engine generation
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not let multiple controllers write one animation channel or infer target-generation priority and fallback semantics from an older example.

steps.action: Treat Model Engine reload or reimport and any integration reload or disable-enable transition explicitly supported by the target deployment as generation changes that invalidate cached blueprint, active-model, animation, and adapter references; do not assume arbitrary server reload is safe. Resolve and verify the candidate as far as the target adapter permits, then use a target-supported replacement transaction: attach and verify before switching when generations may coexist, or first unpublish and retire the old attachment and remain fail-closed if the new attach fails when they may not. Publish at one explicit point, fence old callbacks, and release every old runtime reference. For teleport, follow the target Paper completion and ownership rules, then revalidate the current generation and perform only the resync or reattach required by the verified adapter. Despawn and plugin disable use idempotent cleanup that closes admission, rejects old-generation callbacks, ends animation ownership, detaches or destroys models, releases registrations and references, and either removes an integration-owned carrier or restores only binding-owned properties on a borrowed carrier without deleting it. Cleanup continues through independent failures and leaves a bounded, authoritative registry rather than discovering owned state through broad world scans.
evidence: A target-supported generation-replacement diagram with candidate verification, one publication point, coexistence or fail-closed cutover policy, old-generation fencing, and ordered retirement
Target-version evidence for the Paper teleport, entity ownership, and plugin lifecycle surfaces actually used
